6bce93250afcd3cc: BATU PAHAT: A palm oil worker who threatened and chased his wife with a parang after accusing her of having an affair was sentenced to nine months' jail by the magistrate's court here today.
Magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno imposed the sentence on Ahmad Fairus Mohamed, 42, after he pleaded guilty and after considering the mitigation plea and submissions by the prosecution and defence.
The court ordered the sentence to run from the date of his arrest on Oct 18.
According to the charge, Fairus, who has three children, committed criminal intimidation against his 37-year-old wife using a parang at a house in Senggarang here about 8.30am on Oct 18.
He was charged under Section 506 of the Penal Code, which provides for a jail term of up to seven years, a fine, or both, upon conviction.
According to the case facts, the incident occurred after the complainant, who is also the victim, had an argument with the accused.
The accused then scolded and threatened her before taking a parang from a room and chasing her.
The victim fled to a neighbour's house for help before lodging a police report at the Senggarang police station on the same day, fearing for her safety.
Following the report, police arrested the accused about 1.30pm that day to facilitate investigations.
Deputy public prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim prosecuted, while Kamarularifiin Nordin from the National Legal Aid Foundation represented Fairus.
edb0f3b762a82ddd: KUALA LUMPUR: Customs officers have seized 9,286 electrical appliances worth more than RM1.33 million, including duties and taxes, in a raid on a warehouse in Seri Kembangan, Selangor.
A local man in his 60s, who managed the warehouse, was detained to assist investigations into the suspected smuggling of electrical appliances without the required approvals.
Kuala Lumpur Customs director Wan Norizan Wan Daud said the raid was conducted at a private warehouse in Bukit Belimbing on Oct 13, following intelligence received from the department's headquarters.
4087d99ec51c4e4a: KUALA LUMPUR: Perikatan Nasional has secured a temporary reprieve after the High Court today granted its application to stay the action taken by the Registrar of Societies (RoS), despite the coalition's registration having been cancelled two days ago.
The decision comes just nine days before nomination day for the Melaka election, with the coalition seeking to preserve its right to contest under its own name and symbol.
High Court judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad ruled that the cancellation of PN's registration on Oct 20 did not automatically render its application for a stay academic.
He said the court found exceptional circumstances warranting the stay, particularly the potential harm to PN's political activities and its participation in the upcoming election.
Azizan said the court must consider the greater prejudice that could arise if the stay were granted or refused.
ea4c62bd64978408: PETALING JAYA: Waze menepis dakwaan ia mengumpul maklumat sensitif kerajaan atau membenarkan mana-mana pihak mengeksploitasi data peribadi pengguna selepas Malaysia melarang penjawat awam menggunakan aplikasi itu ketika menjalankan tugas rasmi.
Jurucakap syarikat itu berkata, dakwaan berkenaan "tidak benar sama sekali".

"Waze beroperasi di bawah dasar privasi ketat bagi melindungi data pengguna dan mematuhi piawaian perlindungan data undang-undang global," katanya dalam kenyataan yang dihantar melalui e-mel kepada FMT.
Perdana Menteri, Anwar Ibrahim, melarang penjawat awam menggunakan Waze ketika menjalankan tugas rasmi atas kebimbangan keselamatan berkaitan aplikasi itu tertakluk kepada undang-undang Israel.

Tiada larangan dikenakan terhadap orang awam untuk menggunakan Waze, tetapi Anwar menggalakkan rakyat Malaysia beralih kepada alternatif tempatan seperti TuJu, yang dibangunkan Lembaga Lebuhraya Malaysia dan Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd.
Anwar berkata, larangan itu bagi "melindungi maklumat kerajaan dan data peribadi pengguna daripada ancaman penyalahgunaan oleh rejim Israel".
Syarikat induk Google, Alphabet memperoleh Waze pada Jun 2013 dengan nilai kira-kira USD1.15 bilion. Aplikasi itu diasaskan di Israel pada 2008 oleh tiga usahawan Israel.

Terdahulu, Ketua Pengarah Majlis Keselamatan Negara, Raja Nushirwan Zainal Abidin, hari ini memberi amaran maklumat dikumpul Waze, termasuk lokasi dan pergerakan perjalanan pengguna boleh digunakan untuk mengenal pasti rutin harian mereka.
Bagi penjawat awam, beliau berkata, perkara ini boleh menjadi isu sangat sensitif.
97dcfe7fb6eb57ab: RANTAU PANJANG: The General Operations Force has recorded 11 cases of concertina wire being cut along the Malaysia-Thailand border in Kelantan between March 27 and Oct 12 this year.

Internal Security and Public Order Department deputy director (GOF) Datuk Mohamad Suzrin Mohamad Rodhi said enforcement action had been taken by the GOF and the respective district police headquarters in connection with the incidents.
He said the incidents were believed to involve deliberate acts aimed at creating entry and exit routes through the border fence to facilitate smuggling activities.
"I believe the parties responsible have been identified based on the information gathered," he told reporters this during a visit to the border here today.
Accompanying him was GOF Southeast Brigade commander Datuk Ahmad Radzi Hussain.

Suzrin said GOF would continue to update field intelligence in collaboration with the National Security Council and the relevant police contingents on border intrusions involving the cutting of concertina wire.
He said those on duty would continue repairing cut sections of the wire to restore security control as quickly as possible.

It was learnt that the illegal jetties associated with the cut concertina wire were identified as Abe Li Posmen, Salleh, Kak Mah, Pok Mat, Adam, Abe Yie, Poksu Roni, Syed Agil, Lan Bundle, Cik Ma, Epek, Zin Merah and Gergaji.
It was also learnt that the estimated length of damaged concertina wire at each location is between two and five metres.
e9d271613702ef1e: DAMMAM: Two people were killed and eight were injured in an attack on Wednesday evening on King Fahd International Airport in Saudi Arabia's eastern oil city of Dammam, Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation said on Thursday.
Those killed were a Saudi citizen and an Indian national, the authority said. The injuries ranged from minor to serious.
Damage was being assessed, it added.
Airport operations had resumed and air traffic had returned to normal, the authority said.
Earlier, the Saudi energy ministry said that falling debris from the succesful interception of a drone targeting an oil facility killed two people and injured a further two on Wednesday.
"The attempted attack resulted in the deaths of two individuals, a Filipino and a Nepali, and injuries to two others," the ministry said in a statement.
It did not say who launched the drone aimed at Shaybah oil field near the UAE border.
86b9a96c9f917d18: KUALA LUMPUR: Mahkamah Tinggi membenarkan permohonan Perikatan Nasional (PN) untuk menangguhkan pelaksanaan keputusan Jabatan Pendaftaran Pertubuhan (JPPM) yang membatalkan pendaftaran gabungan itu.
Keputusan itu membolehkan PN bertanding pada PRN Melaka, 14 Nov depan menggunakan nama dan lambang gabungan berkenaan.
Hakim Azizan Arshad berkata penangguhan itu berkuat kuasa sehingga permohonan semakan kehakiman PN terhadap keputusan JPPM diputuskan sepenuhnya.
“Permohonan untuk menangguhkan pelaksanaan dibenarkan sehingga selesai sepenuhnya pendengaran kes, tanpa perintah mengenai kos,” katanya.
8ba5f6cac146dd66: SEREMBAN, Oct 22 — The RM1,000 special financial assistance from the Madani Government has brought relief to more than 400 taxi and hire car drivers in Negeri Sembilan, particularly those celebrating Deepavali, by helping them prepare for the festival, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said.
He said the aid would help reduce recipients’ financial burden, allowing them to meet the costs of Deepavali preparations and their families’ daily needs.
“The RM1,000 may not resolve every problem or fully cover vehicle maintenance costs.
“However, I hope the assistance will go some way towards easing their daily expenses, helping them buy groceries, replace tyres or refuel their vehicles so they can continue earning a living.
“I promised earlier that the assistance would be delivered before Deepavali.

“Today, I am handing it over ahead of the festival so that you can put it towards your Deepavali expenses,” he said at a ceremony for taxi, hire car and school bus drivers at the Seremban City Council Hall today.
Loke said the next phase of the assistance would be paid directly into the bank accounts of other eligible recipients nationwide through electronic funds transfer.

He said the Ministry of Transport (MOT) would continue supporting taxi drivers through its transformation programme to keep them competitive in the public transport industry, including by working with Proton to lower the cost of new vehicles and providing financing facilities and rebates to ease their financial burden.

He said more than 100 vehicles had been booked under the programme, which seeks to boost drivers’ earnings by offering advertising space inside vehicles and using apps to connect them with passengers.

In a related development, Loke said the government would continue to issue special vehicle registration number series, typically two to three a year, but had no plans to introduce numbers featuring specific names or words, opting to retain the existing alphanumeric system.
Loke said the MOT had decided to retain the country’s long-standing vehicle registration system, despite the potential for personalised number plates to generate additional government revenue.
Meanwhile, taxi driver L. Jagathesan, 68, who has worked in the industry for 30 years, said the incentive was the biggest he had received and would go towards his Deepavali expenses.
Port Dickson taxi driver M. Selvaraju, 66, who has worked in the industry for 37 years, said he appreciated the government’s gesture towards taxi drivers and hoped similar efforts would continue.
Driver Muhammad Auzai Azman, 28, who has been in the profession for two years, said the assistance helped drivers like him meet their daily needs. — Bernama
4b1e67a624c571c9: PETALING JAYA: Adun Kampung Tunku Lim Yi Wei menggesa orang ramai agar berhenti menularkan video insiden keganasan di sekolah menerusi media sosial, selain meminta pihak media tidak mensensasikan kejadian sedemikian.

Wakil rakyat DAP itu berkata, gesaan tersebut bertujuan membendung penularan sosial, apabila tingkah laku, emosi, atau idea merebak secara pantas dan spontan, sekali gus berisiko mencetuskan perbuatan 'copycat'.
“Berbincang secara bersemuka mahupun dalam talian serta berkongsi maklumat mungkin dilihat membantu, namun di manakah batas antara tanda solidariti dengan sensasi?” soalnya dalam kenyataan.
Sebelum ini, polis Sarawak mengesahkan remaja yang didakwa menyerang seorang guru di Sekolah Antarabangsa Tunku Putra-HELP di Kuching pagi semalam telah menyiarkan insiden itu secara langsung.

Pemangku pesuruhjaya polis Sarawak Saifullizan Ishak berkata, rakaman berdurasi 12 minit enam saat itu memaparkan serangan dari sudut pandangan suspek, dan video tersebut telah diturunkan oleh Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (SKMM).
Lim turut menzahirkan kekecewaan terhadap hantaran media sosial mengenai insiden di Kuching itu yang menggunakan tanda pagar '#viralkan' dan '#fyp' semata-mata untuk meningkatkan capaian.
“Tindakan itu mengeksploitasi rasa terkejut serta kebimbangan masyarakat terhadap keselamatan sekolah, demi meraih 'likes', perkongsian, dan ada kalanya pendapatan buat pemilik akaun,” katanya.

Lim memetik kajian di Amerika Syarikat pada 2015 yang mendapati pembunuhan beramai-ramai membabitkan senjata api, termasuk insiden tembakan di sekolah, didorong oleh kejadian serupa yang berlaku sebelum itu, dengan peningkatan risiko sementara berlarutan purata selama 13 hari.

“Di luar tempoh ini pula, pelaku pembunuhan beramai-ramai yang amat mengerikan, seperti di Virginia Tech, Sandy Hook dan Umpqua Community College, secara terang-terangan mengakui mengambil inspirasi daripada pelaku terdahulu,” katanya.

Beliau berkata, perbincangan mengenai keganasan di sekolah tidak sepatutnya melibatkan perkongsian video atau mensensasikan tindakan mahupun manifesto penyerang, namun platform media sosial dilihat kurang berminat menurunkan kandungan sedemikian kerana model perniagaan mereka bergantung kepada wacana hangat serta tularan.
“Kita sering kata kanak-kanak mudah terdedah kepada pengaruh media sosial, sedangkan (teori) penularan sosial membuktikan golongan dewasa juga tidak kebal," katanya.
“Kita perlu muhasabah diri: Adakah kita kongsi kerana benar-benar peduli, atau kerana otak kita mendambakan lonjakan endorfin yang diperoleh daripada pengiktirafan di alam maya?”
f7c33d21b48d026d: OCTOBER 22 — As Malaysian universities prepare to welcome a new academic year, campuses across the country will once again become places where students from different parts of the world come together to study, build friendships and experience Malaysia.
This is also a timely moment to think about where Malaysia’s international higher education sector is heading.

Malaysia has set an ambitious goal of attracting 500,000 international students by 2035 as part of its ambition to strengthen its position as a global education hub. The target represents a significant expansion from the 159,138 international students enrolled in Malaysian public and private higher education institutions in 2025.
But as Malaysia seeks to attract more international students, perhaps we should also ask a simpler question: where should these students come from?
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Malaysia has already built a strong international student base. In 2025, China was the largest source of international students, followed by Indonesia, Bangladesh, India and Pakistan. Students from these five countries together accounted for more than half of international enrolment. — Picture by Miera Zulyana
More than numbers

Malaysia has already built a strong international student base. In 2025, China was the largest source of international students, followed by Indonesia, Bangladesh, India and Pakistan. Students from these five countries together accounted for more than half of international enrolment.

The growth of the Chinese student market, in particular, has been an important success story. Malaysia offers Chinese students relatively affordable education, geographical proximity, English-medium programmes and a multicultural environment. These advantages are unlikely to disappear.
But a successful market should not become the only market we depend on.

International education, like tourism, is influenced by changing economic conditions, exchange rates, visa policies, competition and student preferences. A broader international student base can therefore make Malaysia’s higher education sector more resilient.

This does not mean attracting fewer students from China or any other established market. Rather, it means creating more opportunities for students from countries and regions that are currently less represented in Malaysian classrooms.

Malaysia already has a strong foundation for this. The country has welcomed students from 178 nations, demonstrating that its international education appeal is already much broader than the numbers from its largest markets might suggest.
The challenge is to turn that diversity into sustained growth.
Looking beyond traditional markets
Malaysia’s location gives it a natural advantage.

As an Asian country with strong connections to Southeast Asia, South Asia, the Middle East and beyond, Malaysia does not necessarily need to compete with traditional education destinations by trying to replicate their models.
Instead, it can build on what makes Malaysia different.

Affordability remains an important consideration. English is widely used in higher education. Malaysia’s multicultural society also gives international students an opportunity to experience different cultures within a relatively accessible environment.
These advantages can help Malaysia position itself not simply as another destination for international students, but as a gateway to Asia.

This is particularly relevant as higher education becomes increasingly connected to regional mobility. Students today are not only choosing where to study. They are also thinking about where they can build networks, gain international experience and develop careers.
Malaysia can benefit from this trend by broadening its recruitment efforts across Asean, South Asia, the Middle East, Central Asia and Africa.
But recruitment is only one part of the equation.
Attracting students is only the beginning
If Malaysia wants to reach 500,000 international students, universities will need to think beyond how to attract them.
The experience after arrival matters just as much.

Visa processing, accommodation, academic support, campus integration and career opportunities all influence how students perceive a country as an education destination. Malaysia’s new Higher Education Blueprint itself recognises the importance of a world-class learner experience, smoother administrative processes, credit transfer and more inclusive and multicultural learning environments.
This is where diversification can become more than a recruitment strategy.

A more diverse campus benefits international students, but it also benefits Malaysian students. Studying alongside classmates from different countries can expose young Malaysians to different perspectives, cultures and ways of thinking without requiring them to leave the country.
International students, meanwhile, can become long-term bridges between Malaysia and their home countries.

They may return home as alumni, join Malaysian companies, build businesses or maintain academic and professional partnerships. In this sense, international education is not simply about tuition fees or student numbers. It is also about building long-term people-to-people connections.
As a new academic year begins, Malaysian universities will once again welcome students from around the world.
The ambition should certainly be to welcome more.

But perhaps the bigger ambition should be to welcome more diverse communities of students, while giving each of them a reason to choose Malaysia, stay connected to Malaysia and remember Malaysia long after graduation.
If Malaysia wants to become a truly international education hub, its classrooms should not only be larger. They should also reflect the diversity of the world that Malaysia hopes to connect.

* Gareth Liu Zi Yuan is a senior research associate from the Department of South-east Asian Studies, Universiti Malaya. His research expertise focuses on Malaysia studies, Malaysia-Sino relations, and Asean affairs.

6f881a4b9809b737: CEUTA: Mari Carmen Mata remains furious with Spanish prime minister Pedro Sanchez over his response to the mass arrival of migrants in Ceuta, a crisis complicating the Socialist leader's bid for re-election next month.
"We want nothing to do with him," the 58-year-old nursing assistant told AFP in the centre of the Spanish territory in north Africa.
More than two months after upwards of 70,000 migrants entered Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco on July 30 and 31, life in the city, home to around 80,000 people, remains far from normal.
Most returned to Morocco in the following hours, but thousands have remained for weeks in often dire conditions.
A sense of abandonment among residents is giving fresh ammunition to the main opposition conservative Popular Party (PP) and the far-right Vox ahead of an early general election on November 29.

Criticism in Ceuta – governed by the PP for more than 25 years – centres largely on the central government's migration policy and what many see as a lack of firmness towards Morocco, which claims sovereignty over the territory.

"We thought our government was going to do something in the short or medium term, but we've been here for two months and these people haven't been sent back," said Ruben Gonzalez, gesturing towards groups of migrants still wandering through the city.
"Catholics, Muslims, Jews, Hindus – we're all on the same page. We feel abandoned here," added the 33-year-old civil servant.
Gonzalez describes himself as a centrist voter but said he would vote for the right in the coming election.
Sonsoles Jimenez, a 51-year-old businesswoman, agreed, saying "in any other country they wouldn't have allowed what is permitted here in Spain".
'Hybrid attack'
The unprecedented migrant surge dominated headlines in Spain for weeks, with the right accusing Sanchez – one of Europe's last remaining socialist leaders – of being soft on immigration.
His left-wing government had already faced criticism over its decision to open a path to legal status for hundreds of thousands of undocumented foreign residents.
PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo made Ceuta his first campaign stop, pledging to help restore "normality" to the territory.
The leader of Vox, Santiago Abascal, visited Ceuta a few days later on Oct 12, Spain's national day, alongside Jordan Bardella, leader of France's ascendant far-right National Rally party.
Sanchez has no plans, for now, to return to Ceuta, after a brief visit on July 31.
He did not accompany King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia on their historic visit to the city last week.
"The government made a mistake by treating this crisis as a migration crisis. It wasn't just that: it was a hybrid attack," political scientist Cristina Monge told AFP.
She was echoing critics who accused Morocco of deliberately allowing or encouraging the migrant surge to challenge Spain's sovereignty over Ceuta and Melilla, its other north African territory.
Both the Moroccan government and Sanchez rejected the allegations.
'Defend our city'
A September poll published by the El Pais daily found that 63 percent of Spaniards rated Sanchez's handling of the Ceuta surge negatively, including 50% who described it as "very bad".
But the eviction of 87-year-old pensioner Maricarmen Abascal from her lifelong Madrid home has helped shift the political debate towards Spain's housing crisis instead.
The issue has sparked nationwide protests and could give Sanchez, in office since 2018, a boost ahead of the election.

The PP and Vox are pushing to put "immigration, the crisis in Ceuta, Morocco and corruption" at the centre of the campaign, while left-wing parties are trying to shift attention towards housing, social rights and pensions, Monge said.
"Public debate is now focused on social issues," she said. "If the campaign continues along these lines, the question of Ceuta will eventually slip into second or even third place."
That prospect worries many residents of Ceuta.
"What we want is to be able to defend our city, and for Spain and Europe to defend what belongs to them," Jimenez said.
ed8cc56ad5ac852e: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court has granted a stay on the Registrar of Societies' (RoS) decision to deregister Perikatan Nasional (PN), allowing the coalition to contest the upcoming Melaka polls under its banner.
Justice Azizan Arshad said the stay remains in effect until a decision is made on PN's judicial review against the RoS.
"The application for a stay of execution is allowed pending the full disposal of the hearing, with no order as to costs," he said.
9ef72307505efdb0: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 22 — Nine men were charged in the Sessions Court here today with being members of an organised crime group known as the ‘Geng Suria’.

They are Thayalan, 28; A. Tana Balan, 30; Muhamad Rizwan Abd Jalil, 28; G. Sritharan, 39; B. Saranraj, 38; A. Simon, 34; G. Suria Prasad (alleged to be the gang leader), 30; A. Suresh, 52; and Kavines, 31.
No pleas were recorded after the charges were read out in Tamil before Judges Nabisha Ibrahim and Najwa Che Mat in separate courtrooms, as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
The nine men are charged with being members of the organised crime group at an unnumbered house on Jalan Sekerat, Pekan Lama, here, between December 2024 and April this year.
The charge, framed under Section 130V(1) of the Penal Code, provides imprisonment of up to 20 years upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by Deputy Public Prosecutors Yazid Mustaqim Roslan and Mohd Fakhrurrazi Ahmad Salim.
Lawyer S. Sagthiyaraj represented Saranraj and Thayalan, while lawyer Mohammad Naim Kamaruddin represented Sritharan, Simon, and Tana Balan.
The remaining four accused were unrepresented.
The court denied bail to all nine accused and set Nov 17 for mention. — Bernama
1143d246676a01c3: BROUGHT to tears as he recalled Israeli settlers hitting his cherished olive trees with sticks and taking off with the olives, Palestinian Ahmed Salem said he feared being attacked if he tried to intervene.

Settlers have intimidated Palestinians harvesting their olives in the occupied West Bank for decades, but this year, not only has violence increased sharply, theft has been widespread, according to Palestinians, Israeli rights groups and the UN.

The settlers dumped Salem's olives into sacks and then drove them to a nearby Israeli settler outpost to be pressed into olive oil, the 50-year-old Palestinian told Reuters of the incident around two weeks ago near his village Lubban al-Gharbi.
"How would you feel if something that belonged to you was being violated, and you could do nothing about it?" he asked.

The couple living in the outpost, whose olive press settlers have urged Israelis to use for West Bank olives, declined multiple Reuters requests for comment, while the Yesha Council, which oversees Israeli settlements in the West Bank, did not immediately respond.

The attacks have accelerated ahead of an Israeli election next week that opinion polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his pro-settler coalition could lose to opponents who have taken a more critical stance against settler violence.
The olive harvest starts with the onset of cooler weather, allowing Palestinian families to gather in the lush, terraced groves that they have groomed for generations.
"My six-year-old son remembers going there with me, eating there, making tea there," Salem said.

With the establishment of hundreds of small settler outposts under Netanyahu's government since 2022, the military has increasingly restricted Palestinian access to areas nearby, including many olive groves.

"This creates a situation where Palestinians, in many of the cases, many of the lands, especially in proximity to settlements and outposts, cannot enter the land and harvest the trees," said Ziv Stahl, executive director of Israeli rights group Yesh Din.
"But settlers can come and go freely, and that's what they do."
Even when Palestinians can access their trees, it is not without risk.

Yesh Din on Wednesday reported 125 physical attacks on Palestinian olive harvesters over the 24 days since the season began and 168 incidents of crop theft, with Israeli military forces present in at least a quarter of cases.
An Israeli military official said it takes acts of violence, criminal activity and attempts to undermine security very seriously.

The official did not refer to settlers or comment on the reports of olive theft in the presence of the Israeli military, which has separately uprooted trees with excavators, citing what it said was a need to prevent Palestinian attacks.
The removal of Palestinians' olives has met with widely differing responses from Israeli rabbis.
"I call it theft. From my perspective, I define it as theft or robbery, and it is forbidden," said Zev Weitman, the rabbi for the Alon Shvut settlement south of Bethlehem.

Prominent Orthodox rabbi Dov Lior said settlers should harvest across the West Bank, asserting in an open letter that Palestinians had no ownership rights to the land and that harvesting olives fulfilled "the commandment of conquering the land."

Hundreds of acres of the land around Salem's village, Lubban al-Gharbi, including olive groves, were fenced off and seized between 2023 and 2026 by Avichai Farm, an Israeli settler outpost built on a nearby hill.
Salem said villagers have seen settlers harvest olives from the seized land and take them to the outpost's olive press.
At the start of the olive harvest, settlers posted on social media calling on Israelis to harvest West Bank olives and bring them to Avichai Farm's press.
"Both fine oil and strengthening the Jewish hold on the vast expanses of our land!," read a message on a settler Telegram group. "It's either us or our enemy!"

The press at Avichai Farm advertises "premium products produced by Avichai Farm" with olive oil at about US$20 a bottle via a website run by the Farms Association, a settler group that Reuters has reported receives significant financial support from the Israeli government, which says the aim is to promote peace.

The Farms Association did not immediately respond to a request for comment and the couple who live on the farm with their children declined to be interviewed by a Reuters reporter who approached the area on Sunday.

On a road leading to Avichai Farm, Reuters spoke to a man who declined to be identified and said he had driven from a settlement around 90 minutes away to press 14 bags of olives from trees he said he grew himself.
Lubban al-Gharbi villagers and other Palestinians who have lost land to settler expansion say the harvesting of olives from trees in groves seized from Palestinian land constitutes theft.

UN bodies and most countries deem Israel's settlements on land occupied in war illegal under international law regarding military occupations. Israel rejects this, viewing the territory as disputed rather than occupied.

During this year's olive harvest, Palestinian authorities say three Palestinians have been killed in daily militant settler attacks, which have also injured several journalists, European diplomats and a French mayor.
Stahl from the Yesh Din Israeli rights group said the violence was "part of a campaign of ethnic cleansing, paving the way for the annexation of the West Bank without its Palestinian population."
Israel, which has considered the idea of annexation, said it is investigating some of the incidents.

An Israeli government spokesperson said olives "picked by a Jew in the ancestral homeland of the Jewish people" did not constitute theft and that Jews owned and cultivated "millions of olive trees" in the area. No one should take the law into their own hands, the spokesperson added.

Palestinian farmer Samer Ben Shamsi said masked settlers attacked him on Oct 9 in the Palestinian village of Beita near Nablus, then sped away in a pickup truck with his harvest of olives after he and other farmers fled.
"This year, they steal without fear because they have a state and a powerful force backing them," Ben Shamsi said, referring to the security forces.
Within the past year alone, settlers had shot him in the leg, beaten him and smashed his possessions, he said.
"We pay in blood for the olives."
* The writers are from Reuters

8a942047ec297ca4: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Malaysia is strengthening its energy partnership with Turkmenistan to unlock new commercial opportunities for companies, particularly in higher-value oil and gas services, technology and specialised engineering, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.

“Our companies are ready to work with Turkmenistan partners not only as suppliers, but as long-term collaborators committed to local value creation,” the minister said in his remarks during the opening plenary of the Oil and Gas of Turkmenistan 2026 in Ashgabat.

The three-day OGT 2026, which began on Oct 21, brought together 20 Malaysian oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) companies, including Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas), according to a statement by the Economy Ministry today.

Of these, seven exhibitors were at the inaugural Malaysia Pavilion, under the National OGSE Industry Blueprint 2021-2030’s International Market Access Programme led by Malaysia Petroleum Resources Corporation (MPRC).

The ministry said the engagement builds on Petronas’ 30-year presence in Turkmenistan and follows the formalisation of the Framework Agreement on Long-Term Cooperation for the Development of Hydrocarbon Resources in Turkmenistan during Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s official visit in June 2026.

“Industry cooperation is set to be further strengthened through a memorandum of understanding between MPRC and (Turkmenistan’s national oil company) State Concern Turkmennebit, scheduled to be signed today, to facilitate collaboration in OGSE in Turkmenistan,” it said.

As part of the visit, Akmal Nasrullah is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with Turkmenistan’s Deputy Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers Guvanch Agajanov, State Minister and SC Turkmengas chairman Maksat Babayev, Finance and Economy Minister Mammetguly Astanagulov, and the leadership of Dragon Oil and Eni Turkmenistan Ltd to strengthen bilateral economic ties and explore strategic collaboration.

“These engagements will build the momentum for the Malaysia-Turkmenistan Energy Cooperation Roundtable, bringing together Malaysian OGSE companies and Turkmenistan’s key stakeholders, including Turkmengas and Turkmennebit.

“The roundtable is expected to translate shared interests into concrete cooperation focusing on high-value services, technology transfer and skills development, in line with the 13th Malaysia Plan (2026-2030),” the ministry added. — Bernama
b04d1f2b488ce5e1: GEORGE TOWN: Penang will submit its action plan and supporting papers for the proposed Penang Technology Financial Centre (PTFC) to the Finance Ministry in November.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said state government officers and the State Finance Department would engage with the ministry on the next steps to advance the proposal.
"We will submit the action plan and the papers we need in November," he told reporters after the Penang International Science Fair.
Chow said further discussions with senior ministry officials were expected after the 2027 Budget debate and approval process was completed.
"The discussions will focus on initiating the necessary work to implement the proposal," he said.

He said the proposed centre had also been referred to as the National Technology Financial Centre during discussions, adding that the state was open to the initiative being established as a national-level centre.
"For now, we are still using the temporary name as further discussions need to be held," he said.

In his 2027 Budget speech, Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced plans to develop Penang as a national technology hub, supported by a RM100 million fund established by Khazanah Nasional Bhd and InvestPenang for early-stage semiconductor and advanced manufacturing companies.

Following the announcement, Chow said the state would continue discussions with the Finance Ministry on establishing a federal-state joint committee to coordinate planning, implementation and follow-up action.
2ed354d28122b429: KUALA LUMPUR: National singles coaching director Kenneth Jonassen is keeping his cool amid the national men's singles players' poor performances.
Jonassen is in no rush to make drastic decisions and instead, the Dane prefers to conduct an assessment of his players' performances and progress before making key changes at the end of the year.
The national men's singles department has struggled to deliver encouraging results, with Leong Jun Hao suffering first-round exits at both the Denmark Open and French Open.
Jonassen said he refused to let the success of the national doubles players put additional pressure on his singles squad, preferring to remain positive as he works to improve their performances.
"We are currently evaluating the results and progress of the players throughout this year. Towards the end of the year, we will make some changes and decisions to strengthen the team.

"As for how I feel personally, I do not allow myself to feel that kind of pressure. I choose to take a positive approach because it is very important for us to keep moving forward," he said when contacted.
World No. 31 Jun Hao crashed out in the opening round of the French Open after losing to Japan's Koki Watanabe.
Jun Hao also suffered a first-round defeat to the same opponent at the Denmark Open last week.
The Malaysian has endured a difficult season, having also made early exits at the Badminton Asia Championships, World Championships and the men's singles event at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.
e040c94d67f805c4: SYDNEY: A probe into KPMG Australia has found it mishandled whistleblower allegations of client data leaks and let cultural and governance weaknesses persist for years, but stopped short of recommending a permanent ban on the firm from federal government work.

The finance department, which commissioned the review by former bureaucrat Ian Watt, said KPMG has instead agreed to not bid for new federal work until the end of February while the firm undertakes further governance reforms, extending a pause in place since June.

"The review considers that KPMG should not be treated as permanently unsuitable for Commonwealth work, but nor should confidence be restored on the strength of assurances and encouraging early signs alone," it said.
Federal government work made up A$207.1 million, or 9.5%, of KPMG's revenue in the 2026 financial year, the report said.
The review was launched to probe KPMG's suitability for government work following a whistleblower's allegations that staff misused confidential information to bid for new audit contracts.
"KPMG mishandled the whistleblower matter. Its response was misguided, fragmented, prolonged and, at critical points, lacked clear ownership," the report released on Thursday said.
KPMG said it accepted the review's findings and recommendations.
"The report lays bare our failings and highlights the hard work that we must do to address them," it said.
"Confidence in KPMG's suitability for Commonwealth work must be earned through evidence of effective, lasting change."

The report said despite the whistleblower raising concerns of unethical conduct arising from commercial pressure and a fear of retaliation, KPMG primarily treated it as an "employment matter" and was more focused on the legal implications and organisational risks, paying inadequate attention to whether the allegations might be accurate.
KPMG initially said the allegations were unsubstantiated by investigations, before subsequent ones uncovered "serious ethical failings".
"These shortcomings significantly damaged the whistleblower's confidence in KPMG's handling of the claims. It also damaged client and public confidence and KPMG's credibility," it said.
KPMG's mishandling of the whistleblower's complaint also reflected broader weaknesses in its culture and governance, which have persisted for years at the firm.

The report said that by 2020, KPMG had already identified issues around "the primacy of financial returns, inconsistent ethical leadership, reluctance to challenge senior personnel, barriers to reporting misconduct and weaknesses in ethical decision-making". But there was little evidence the firm adequately addressed them, it found.
It recommended the government should not allow KPMG to bid for new contracts again until it independently verified it was implementing reforms and that they were "changing behaviour in practice".
Since the scandal became public in March, KPMG has lost major blue-chip clients and replaced key leaders, including its CEO, chairman and audit chief.
366e6eb9c3ec3f07: GEORGE TOWN: Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow wants clarification on the restriction barring civil servants from using Waze, citing the app's role in helping motorists navigate traffic congestion.
He said Waze had become a useful tool for drivers across Malaysia, helping them find routes to their destinations more efficiently, particularly amid congestion in cities and towns.
He said the restriction had raised questions among the public, with many seeking to understand the reasons behind the decision.
"The use of Waze has become an important part of driving for everyone, as it is an application that helps them reach their destinations in the fastest way.
"A clearer explanation will help motorists understand the rationale behind the restriction, including whether suitable alternatives are available.
"They need to explain why it has to be banned, why it cannot be used and whether there is a better alternative," he told reporters after announcing the Penang International Science Fair.
It was reported that the government had directed all civil servants to stop using the Waze navigation app with immediate effect.
The decision was made at a National Cyber Security Committee meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday.
Anwar had encouraged the public to use TuJu, a local navigation app developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority, as an alternative.
The move was prompted by concerns over information security and the collection of Malaysians' movement data, as Waze is subject to Israeli laws.
Chow said Waze had proven useful to motorists and made daily journeys more convenient, especially in areas affected by traffic congestion.
Asked whether the Penang state government had received the directive, Chow said he understood that it had reached his driver, but the state government had yet to receive it.
ba34c1c8ccce21d2: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The government is finalising the Natural Gas Roadmap (NGR) to guide the coordinated development of Malaysia’s gas sector in line with national policies and the 13th Malaysia Plan, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.
“I wish to thank all stakeholders who have contributed to this process.
“A roadmap will matter only if it translates into projects, reforms and measurable outcomes,” he said in his pre-recorded video for the Malaysian Gas Symposium (MyGAS) 2026 today.
He said Malaysia must strengthen its gas supply resilience amid global market uncertainty and rising energy demand from advanced manufacturing, data centres and digital industries.
“We have seen how quickly global conditions can change.
“Disruptions to international liquefied natural gas (LNG) trade this year have affected availability and heightened price volatility across our region.
“The lesson is straightforward: Malaysia must not depend on favourable global market conditions.
“We must strengthen our own resilience — through diversified supply, sound procurement, infrastructure readiness and effective market arrangements.

“This means supporting the development of domestic gas resources, diversifying sources of imported LNG to complement domestic supply, and ensuring that infrastructure is available to deliver gas to consumers,” he said.

He said the development of domestic gas resources must account for the differing resource positions and development needs of peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak, in collaboration with the respective state governments and relevant industry players.

As a country that both produces and imports gas, he said Malaysia must also continue to strengthen relationships with supplying countries and regional partners, while maintaining its standing as a reliable participant in international gas trade.
Akmal Nasrullah said natural gas would remain important for electricity system flexibility, industrial production and high-value economic activities.

Under the National Energy Transition Roadmap’s Responsible Transition pathway, natural gas is projected to account for 56 per cent of Malaysia’s total primary energy supply by 2050, supporting reliable electricity supply as renewable energy expands.
The government has agreed to the development of the Third Regasification Terminal (RGT3) in Lumut, Perak, to strengthen Malaysia’s long-term gas supply security.

Targeted to commence commercial operations in the second quarter of 2029, RGT3 is expected to enhance the resilience and flexibility of the country’s gas supply infrastructure, support growing domestic energy demand and reinforce investor confidence in Malaysia’s energy security.
He said technologies such as carbon capture, utilisation and storage as well as biomethane offer further opportunities where they are technically suitable and commercially viable.
“I encourage the industry to demonstrate progress through measurable reductions in emissions.
“We must create more economic value from every unit of gas, while reducing its environmental footprint,” he said.

Meanwhile, Ministry of Economy secretary-general Datuk Seri Nor Azmie Diron said the NGR aims to balance energy security, affordability and environmental sustainability, while also addressing the differing gas development needs in peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.

On new gas infrastructure for peninsular Malaysia, he said the development of the regasification terminal in Lumut, Perak and Yan, Kedah will add more than 1,000 million standard cubic feet per day of capacity, strengthening energy security, particularly across northern peninsular Malaysia.

In Sabah, further investments will focus on developing virtual pipeline systems as well as exploring offshore gas sources on the East Coast and future regasification terminals, in line with the Sabah Energy Roadmap and Master Plan 2040.
“As for Sarawak, the NGR recognises the four gas hubs in Kuching, Bintulu, Samalaju and Miri that have been identified in the Sarawak Gas Roadmap,” he said.
He said the roadmap would also improve gas market efficiency through third-party access and digital systems to facilitate gas trading and capacity booking.

Meanwhile, Malaysian Gas Association (MGA) president Abang Yusuf Abang Puteh said that amid growing global uncertainty and changing energy markets, the focus must now shift from identifying challenges to finding practical solutions that strengthen Malaysia’s energy security, resilience and long-term competitiveness.
He said one key lesson from our experience is that every part of the energy system is interconnected, and our efforts must be equally collaborative.
“Gas supply must reach the people and industries that need it.
“Infrastructure must be reliable and ready for changing demand.
“Projects need investment, and investment depends on confidence.
“Each of us holds part of the solution; progress comes when we bring those parts together,” he said.
MyGAS 2026 is a half-day event organised by MGA, with this year’s theme, “Powering Confidence: Practical Pathways for a Resilient Energy Future”. — Bernama
61ad37b2d4e48ec7: PETALING JAYA: The Malaysian Medical Association (MMA) has urged Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) to disclose what protection is available to patients affected by insurance companies' withdrawal of cashless facilities for private specialists.

In a statement, MMA president Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan also called on the central bank to reveal the number of complaints received over cashless restrictions, panel withdrawals and demands for doctors to return payments, as well as how many cases were resolved.

The MMA’s call follows revelations during the 2027 budget debate in the Dewan Rakyat that about 190 private sector specialist doctors nationwide had reportedly lost their cashless facilities with insurance companies.
Cashless facilities allow insured patients to receive treatment without paying upfront, with the insurer settling the approved medical bill directly with the healthcare provider.
“Healthcare in this country is increasingly being controlled by ‘commercial interests’ rather than guided by clinical judgment and the needs of patients,” he said.

“Malaysians pay their medical insurance premiums every month in good faith. They expect to be covered when they fall ill. Instead, a growing number are told that their chosen specialists have been removed from a panel or restricted from cashless admission.

“They are then forced to change doctors, move hospitals or pay tens of thousands of ringgit upfront. In emergencies, such delays can put lives at risk. Patients must never become collateral damage in commercial disputes involving insurers, hospitals and doctors.”
Sivanaesan called on BNM to establish a transparent framework governing insurers' decisions to restrict doctors' cashless facilities and remove doctors from panels.
The framework should require insurers to provide written reasons and evidence for their decisions, allow doctors to respond and rectify shortcomings, and establish a clear appeal process, he said.
Insurers requiring specialists to work for 1 year before treating insured patients
Sivanaesan also expressed concern over reports that some insurers required newly appointed specialists to work at a private hospital for a year before they could treat insured patients.
He said specialists had already undergone training and received recognition from the relevant authorities.
“It is not the role of an insurance company to override that recognition,” he said.
“When commercial entities decide who may practise and on whom, the doctor-patient relationship is undermined and medicine becomes subordinate to the balance sheet.”
Sivanaesan raised concerns about retrospective audits and clawbacks, in which insurers seek to recover payments for completed cases, sometimes over documentation, coding or administrative issues.
Such actions were often taken without written explanations, supporting evidence or a fair opportunity for doctors to respond, he said.

Sivanaesan urged the health ministry to review and update procedure coding and the medical fee schedule — which he said was a frequent source of disputes — to reflect current clinical practices and technological advances.
He also called for safeguards to ensure patients' treatment continued uninterrupted while disputes involving insurers, hospitals and doctors were being resolved.
Sivanaesan warned that unchecked restrictions could push more patients towards already overburdened government hospitals and weaken the healthcare system.

“Health insurance exists to protect patients, not to obstruct their treatment,” he said, calling for meaningful engagement among all stakeholders and greater patient involvement in decisions affecting their care.
1e8596ab3f200792: WASHINGTON: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he is prepared to freeze the current front lines in a bid to end the conflict, reported German Press Agency (dpa).
"Yes, right now, we have to freeze," he said in an interview with United States (US) broadcaster Fox News on Wednesday. "I think this is [a] real way to end this conflict."

He was responding to a question about whether he would "accept a peace deal that freezes everything the way it is right now, where you still keep 75 per cent or more of your country, regardless of how it started".
"Freeze and stop. And, of course, this is the minimum of what we need from Russia today.
"Then, of course, we will go to [the] president and to Europeans, and we'll ask [for] security guarantees," he said.
Zelenskyy's position is not new. Kyiv has repeatedly proposed halting hostilities along the current front lines.
Moscow has rejected such proposals in the past, arguing that a ceasefire would give Ukraine time to rearm.
Russian President Vladimir Putin has maintained that his troops are advancing, a view that US President Donald Trump has tended to share.
However, Ukrainian forces have halted Russian advances in some areas in recent months and have even pushed Russian troops back in certain sectors.
On Wednesday, US envoy Steve Witkoff presented Putin with new proposals to end the conflict during a meeting in St. Petersburg.
Witkoff had met Zelenskyy and European leaders in Oslo before travelling to Russia, and was expected to return to Oslo for further consultations.
Following the meeting, Moscow said it was ready in principle to resume trilateral talks involving Russia, the US and Ukraine next month. — BERNAMA
7121926d833a24d7: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is awaiting details of Nepal's proposed special order to expedite missing-person and death certificates for victims still unaccounted for following the Aug 26 floods and landslides.
Foreign Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan said the proposed measure would apply specifically to victims of the disaster and would not cover previous missing-person cases in Nepal.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had contacted his Nepalese counterpart to discuss the proposed measure.
"Under the order, Nepal could shorten the period required to issue missing-person or death certificates from 12 years to 45 days. We are monitoring developments closely.
"We want the executive order or special ordinance to be comprehensive and Malaysia will provide input after reviewing the document.

"The document is necessary because, without it, the victims' families would face difficulties settling various matters," he said in response to a supplementary question from Datuk Mohd Suhaimi Abdullah (Bersatu-Langkawi) in the Dewan Rakyat.
Mohamad said the documents were essential for the victims' next-of-kin to settle matters such as insurance claims, access to bank accounts and other legal affairs.
On Suhaimi's second supplementary question about Malaysia-Nepal diplomatic relations, Mohamad said ties between the two countries remained unaffected by the disaster.
"Malaysia has maintained diplomatic relations with Nepal since independence, and Nepal is a like-minded country.
"Our diplomatic relations have not been affected. In fact, ties have grown closer due to more frequent communication between the two countries," he said.
055e3b9861785754: KUALA LUMPUR: Former national cycling coach Datuk Ng Joo Ngan paid tribute to his elder brother, pioneer Olympic cyclist Ng Joo Pong, who died on Wednesday aged 80.
Joo Ngan described his brother as both a pioneer of Malaysian cycling and the personal hero who inspired him to take up the sport.
"I was very close to him. He was a hero for me, and I started cycling to follow his footsteps," said Joo Ngan.
"He was a great competitor and a pioneer for Malaysian cycling in the 1960s."
Known as the "King of the Road", Joo Pong broke new ground as Malaysia's first cycling representative at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics before competing again at the 1968 Mexico City Games.
He also won bronze in the 10,000m mass start at the 1970 Asian Games in Bangkok, where both brothers represented Malaysia, before retiring from competitive cycling.
Joo Ngan said his brother was remembered for his jovial personality and ability to connect with people from all walks of life.
"He had a great personality and was very jovial, so he made friends easily," said Joo Ngan.
"He had a lot of friends from different backgrounds because of his nature. People were just happy to be around him."
Joo Ngan had made it a point to visit his bedridden brother weekly, travelling from Cheras to Shah Alam to keep him company.
Joo Pong had suffered a second stroke seven years ago and was admitted to Universiti Malaya Medical Centre in April due to low blood pressure.
He had remained bedridden while battling hypertension, diabetes, and stroke-related complications.
"He would be happy whenever he saw me and smile brightly. But in the last few weeks, he looked weak and his speech became softer," said Joo Ngan.
After asking their sister to visit Joo Pong, Joo Ngan briefly held out hope when she reported that their brother seemed to perk up.
"However, he passed away after that. I am devastated by his passing. I will miss him," said Joo Ngan.
Joo Pong leaves behind his wife, Ong Beng Kin, and son, Eric Ng.
The wake will be held at Nirvana 2, 16, Jalan Dewan Bahasa, Bukit Seputeh, Kuala Lumpur, on Saturday and Sunday.
The cortege will leave for cremation at Nirvana Crematorium in Shah Alam on Monday.
89a686650abd4368: HANOI: Developers of a new US-backed undersea data cable linking Malaysia, Vietnam, Singapore and Thailand will this month select a cable supplier between Japan's NEC and France's Alcatel Submarine Networks, a project executive told Reuters.

The 16-fibre-pair MViSTA cable is expected to enter service in late 2028 with an estimated cost of about US$400 million, said Mark Procter, deputy head of Stavian High Tech Infrastructure, a unit of Vietnamese conglomerate Stavian Group and one of the project's developers.
"The project's backers excluded Chinese suppliers from bidding and designed the route to avoid the vast area claimed by Beijing in the South China Sea," Procter said.
"Stavian is also planning a data-centre campus in southern Vietnam linked to the cable, with 'no Chinese company involved in any key technology deployed' in the cluster," he added.

Communist-run Vietnam maintains a delicate balance between major powers and has emerged as a key arena in the competition between US and Chinese technologies, with Washington pressing Hanoi to avoid Chinese vendors in submarine cables, telecoms and AI technology due to concerns about security that could impact investments.
However, Vietnam last year awarded contracts to Chinese telecom firms Huawei and ZTE for parts of its 5G rollout, in a major shift which raised concerns among US and European officials.

MViSTA is backed by the US. APTelecom, a consultancy working with the US government on cable infrastructure, facilitated the formation of the group of shareholders, worked on the feasibility study and is helping secure customers for the cable and the data-centre campus, Procter said.

"Alongside Stavian, the project's shareholders include Tokyo-based investment firm Midas Capital and LitUp Network, a subsidiary of Malaysia's OMS Group, which will be responsible for laying the 2,500-km cable," Procter said.
The cable's estimated cost, supplier shortlist and extent of US involvement are reported here for the first time.

"The tender for the supply of the cable is underway with a decision on the winner slated for later in October," said Procter, who is also the chief operating officer of the special purpose vehicle set up to develop and operate the cable.
ASN said it does not comment on ongoing tendering activity. NEC did not respond to a request for comment.
US cable maker SubCom was also invited to bid but declined because of existing commitments, Procter said.

The project is significant for Vietnam, which is prone to recurring cable outages and plans to expand the number of submarine cables connecting the country to at least 15 by 2030 from six now. Procter said the government sped up approval procedures for the project.
Stavian plans to connect the MViSTA cable to a new campus in southern Vietnam.

The campus is designed to host data centres for "hyperscale cloud and AI infrastructure operators", according to a September statement from the US Trade and Development Agency (USTDA), which is funding a feasibility study.

"The study, due for completion in March 2027, will assess the deployment of trusted technology and evaluate whether US restrictions on exports of advanced semiconductors could affect the planned 1GW infrastructure," Procter said.
The cable-linked campus could address infrastructure constraints that have prevented big US tech firms from investing in data centres in Vietnam.
"However, investments will also depend on Vietnam's regulatory framework," Procter said, with restrictions on cross-border data flows often cited by industry bodies as a key barrier.
1b3a7d06963af4d4: NEW DELHI: India began annual measures on Thursday to tackle toxic air pollution in New Delhi, a megacity of 30 million people regularly ranked among the world's most polluted capitals.
Delhi's air quality deteriorates in winter, when cooler air traps pollutants close to the ground.
Major sources include coal-fired power plants, traffic, construction and farm stubble burning in neighbouring areas.
The Delhi government on Wednesday announced a ban on open rubbish burning and ordered food stalls to stop using coal or firewood.

In previous years, such measures have failed to curb pollution, which peaks from November to January, when levels of cancer-causing PM 2.5 microparticles often hit more than 300 micrograms per cubic metre, 20 times the World Health Organization's recommended daily maximum.
Monitors recorded 233 micrograms per cubic metre early Thursday, about 15 times the limit.
The government's Commission for Air Quality Management has predicted air quality to remain "poor" the coming days.
A study in The Lancet Planetary Health in 2024 estimated that 3.8 million deaths in India between 2009 and 2019 were linked to pollution that exceeded India's own air quality guidelines.
Last year, pollution levels peaked at 846 micrograms per cubic metre, 56 times the WHO limit.
The UN children's agency warns that polluted air puts children at heightened risk of acute respiratory infections.
Further restrictions take effect on November 1, including doubled parking fees and work-from-home arrangements for government office staff, aimed at reducing traffic emissions.
Tighter construction rules will also begin then, followed by a complete ban on construction and demolition from Dec 10 to Jan 20.

33b2bcfca19bbfa8: KUALA LUMPUR: The Communications Ministry is considering a study to assess public understanding of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) and awareness of Sabah and Sarawak's rights, as part of efforts to strengthen understanding of Malaysia's formation.
Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the ministry acknowledged that knowing about the agreement and understanding and recognising the rights it guaranteed were two different things.
She said the ministry would consider the proposal after Isnaraissah Munirah Majlis (Warisan-Kota Belud) raised the matter in the Dewan Rakyat.
"At present, the ministry, through Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM) and the Information Department, has not conducted a study to measure public understanding of MA63 and the formation of Malaysia.
"I will bring the proposal from the Kota Belud MP back for discussion with the ministry and the Information Department to determine whether the study can be conducted," she said.
Isnaraissah had called for a baseline study to assess how well Malaysians, particularly those in Peninsular Malaysia, understood Sabah and Sarawak's rights under MA63.
She said the study would help the government identify more effective ways to raise public awareness of the agreement.

Public understanding remained important, she said, as some Malaysians continued to misunderstand Sabah and Sarawak's demands for their rights, with such claims sometimes portrayed as threats to national interests.
"Some have even gone to the extreme of accusing us of wanting to leave Malaysia.

"The findings are important to ensure that Malaysians not only know about MA63 but also understand and acknowledge the rights of Sabah and Sarawak, as promised to us before we agreed to form the Federation of Malaysia."

In response, Teo cited the Information Department's digital outreach efforts, which included 115 social media posts, 21 of which featured creative content related to Malaysia's formation and the implementation of MA63.
The content had recorded 119,708 views, 13,660 likes and 17,203 shares as of Sept 22, she said.
However, she acknowledged that these figures did not constitute a study measuring public understanding of the agreement.
cd53a155646adcbb: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Malaysia’s projected achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by 2030 has risen to 58 per cent, up from 49 per cent last year, and surpassing the global projection of 35 per cent.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the improvement reflected the country’s progress in advancing the SDG agenda, although further efforts were needed to ensure development benefited all Malaysians.

“To me, the SDGs are not merely about numbers and targets, but a commitment to ensuring national development brings meaningful change to people’s lives, leaving no one behind or marginalised,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Earlier, Anwar chaired the 2026 National SDG Council meeting, which reviewed Malaysia’s progress in implementing the goals.

He said the meeting also assessed progress on 10 key SDG priorities directly affecting public well-being, including child malnutrition, mental health, empowerment of persons with disabilities, environmental sustainability, fraud threats and efforts to narrow development gaps between states. — Bernama
1f9bf5af27776fc3: BEIJING: Chinese President Xi Jinping urged effective qualitative improvement and reasonable quantitative growth in the economy in a speech on Thursday, Xinhua reported.

"We must resolutely promote high-quality development and continuously meet the people’s ever-growing needs for a better life," Xi said about promoting comprehensive social progress while maintaining stability.
He also emphasised upholding the Communist Party of China's "absolute leadership" over the armed forces and advancing the "political building of the military", the state news agency reported.
The leader mentioned reform in the military, and strengthening through science and technology, as well as with talent and lawful governance.

The speech was part of commemorations for the 90th anniversary of the Long March, a series of retreats by the Red Army, led by Mao Zedong, to evade the pursuing Nationalist forces of Chiang Kai-shek in 1934 and 1935.
dacd5ca30deedcd6: BENTONG: The Immigration Department today launched an integrated operation in Janda Baik, following a report by BH more than a week ago on the growing presence of foreigners in the popular tourist destination and traditional village settlement.
The operation, conducted with the Road Transport Department (RTD), began at about 10am, with enforcement teams raiding 19 locations and checking 278 foreigners.

Immigration deputy director-general (Operations) Datuk Lokman Effendi Ramli said 65 foreigners were found to have committed various offences under the Immigration Act 1963, including not having valid passes, overstaying and misusing permits.

The raids covered Kampung Sumsum and Kampung Cheringin, involving three teams from the Pahang, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Immigration offices, as well as RTD, with a total of 150 officers and personnel.

"Raids were also conducted at construction sites, farms and resorts. The 65 foreigners detained, aged between 20 and 54, included nine women. They were taken to the Semenyih Immigration detention depot for further action.

"We also issued two notices requiring premises owners - one a resort owner and the other a farm owner - to appear before the Immigration Department's Investigation Division for further investigation," he said at a press conference attended by Enforcement Division director Datuk Basri Othman.

On Oct 11, BH reported that Janda Baik, long known for its natural beauty and as a popular tourist attraction, was facing an issue involving the presence of migrants from Indonesia, Nepal, Pakistan and Bangladesh.
Information gathered indicated that they were in the area not only as workers but also to explore business and agricultural opportunities.
Lokman Effendi said the department had deployed a team to conduct intelligence gathering for a week following the report before carrying out today's operation.
"Some foreigners tried to flee during the raids, but all were detained. An officer sustained minor injuries while pursuing them.
"We cordoned off the area to ensure they would be apprehended even if they tried to escape. Some were also detained by RTD officers during roadblocks.

"The operation also extended to a construction site at the foot of Gunung Nuang. Preliminary investigations found that some of them had been here for more than four years without valid passes," he said.
He said the presence of foreigners in certain areas was driven by demand.

"We believe ties between the public and the authorities need to be strengthened to facilitate the sharing of information. For example, if foreigners are engaged in farming in an area, the land or premises owner must have given them permission.

"If premises owners or Malaysians themselves were patriotic and refused to allow foreigners to stay or conduct such activities, would they be able to do so? Certainly not. Malaysians themselves must therefore act responsibly.
"There is no need to make it easy for them to stay here for long periods or engage in activities they should not be carrying out on premises under our care," he said.

In a related development, Lokman Effendi said the department had conducted an average of 37 operations daily during the first 10 months of this year, bringing the total to about 11,000 operations so far.

He said about 150,000 foreigners had been checked during the operations, with more than 66,000 detained. Of these, 45,000 had been deported to their home countries, while the rest were still being processed by the Immigration Department and other enforcement agencies.
"Most of the more than 66,000 foreigners detained were from Bangladesh, Indonesia and Myanmar.

"The figures show that Immigration conducts an average of more than 37 raids a day. This means there is hardly an hour without an operation or raid, demonstrating our commitment to detaining foreigners who violate immigration laws," he said.
Arman_NST Business:
He also said the department had identified 224 hotspots nationwide for monitoring issues involving foreigners.
He urged the public to act as the department's "eyes and ears" by providing information to facilitate follow-up action.
"If members of the public witness any violations of the law by foreigners, they should lodge an official report.
"This will enable the relevant authorities to conduct follow-up action and intelligence gathering.
"It is important that we enforce the law through proper legal channels.
"We do not want members of the public taking matters into their own hands, as this could lead to other undesirable incidents," he said.

4f58174b139c7313: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Air Pollutant Index (API) readings issued by the Department of Environment (DOE) remain the government’s official reference for determining air quality and managing haze.

Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the official API was calculated based on the concentrations of six major pollutants monitored around the clock through 68 automatic air quality monitoring stations nationwide.

He said the stations used measurement equipment and technical methods recognised by the United States Environmental Protection Agency, with procedures in place to ensure the accuracy and reliability of the data.

“Station operations include equipment maintenance, calibration, instrument performance checks and quality assurance procedures to ensure that the data used to calculate the official API are accurate and reliable,” he said during the Minister’s Question Time in the Dewan Rakyat today.

Arthur was answering a question from Manndzri Nasib (BN-Tenggara), who wanted to know how the government ensured that Malaysia’s official API readings were accurate, transparent and trusted by the public.

He said the stations operated under a Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP), which included daily automated zero and span checks, periodic calibration using standard gases traceable to international metrology standards under the National Institute of Standards and Technology, and regular performance audits.

Data collected were also monitored continuously through the Environmental Data Centre to detect changes in readings, assess equipment performance and enable corrective action in the event of disruptions or irregularities.

Arthur said the official API was updated hourly, while the calculations for PM2.5 and PM10 were based on their 24-hour moving average concentrations, in line with World Health Organisation standards and practices adopted by international environmental agencies.

On differences between official API readings and those displayed on platforms such as the Air Quality Index (AQI) and other independent applications, he said these did not necessarily mean that the official readings were inaccurate.

“Differences may arise because these platforms use different scales, thresholds, categories, averaging periods, update times and data sources,” he said, adding that some also relied on low-cost sensors or estimates derived from models and satellite data.
He explained that satellite data measured particle concentrations in the atmosphere rather than actual air quality at ground level, where people breathe.
Such readings could also be affected by cloud cover and atmospheric humidity.
Meanwhile, Arthur said the ministry was open to improving the National Haze Action Plan to ensure that coordination mechanisms and protective measures remained relevant as haze conditions changed.

“This is important to ensure that the actions of the various agencies are better coordinated, particularly when API readings reach unhealthy or very unhealthy levels, to protect public health and well-being,” he said.
On measures to address haze and open burning, Arthur said the government maintained a zero-tolerance approach towards open burning.
The DOE had taken 3,433 enforcement actions related to open-burning incidents between August and October this year, he added. — Bernama
5445205b1c413a73: PETALING JAYA: Waze has rejected claims that it collects sensitive government information or allows any party to exploit users' personal data after Malaysia barred civil servants from using the app on official duty.
A company spokesman told FMT in an emailed statement that the claims were "completely false".
"Waze operates under strict privacy policies that protect user data and comply with global legal data protection standards," the spokesman said.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim ordered the ban on Waze for civil servants while on official duty over security concerns linked to the app being subject to Israeli laws.
There is no ban on the public using Waze, although Anwar urged Malaysians to switch to local alternatives such as TuJu, developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority and Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd.
Anwar said the ban was intended "to protect government information and users' personal data from the threat of misuse by the Israeli regime".
Google parent Alphabet acquired Waze in June 2013 for about US$1.15 billion. The app was founded in Israel in 2008 by three Israeli entrepreneurs.

Earlier today, National Security Council director-general Raja Nushirwan Zainal Abidin warned that information collected by Waze, including users' locations and travel movements, could be used to establish their daily routines.
For civil servants, he said that this could be a highly sensitive issue.
0612d3d57897c91b: KUALA LUMPUR: A week into married life, Muar Member of Parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and singer-actress Bella Astillah are happily settling into their new journey together as a blended family with her two children, Ayden and Ara.

Reflecting on his new life as a husband, Syed Saddiq shared that simple everyday moments—like having breakfast together, doing the school run, and spending quality time as a family—have brought him profound joy.
Speaking after their wedding reception at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) recently, he noted that these small routines have made the biggest difference.
"The biggest and most positive change is waking up to have my wife by my side, along with two children whom I can eat breakfast with and send to school," he said in a Berita Harian report today.

"When I come home, sometimes exhausted after a long day at Parliament, the kids are there to greet me. We can even work out together. It's these little things that bring about a massive transformation in life."
For Bella, the early days of marriage have been all about adjusting to life under one roof with Syed Saddiq and establishing new daily routines for their family of four.

"I moved into my husband's house with the kids, so we had to establish a new routine together. So far, praise be to God, everything has been going smoothly. We still have a long journey ahead, and I just hope for the best, God willing," she remarked.
Bella added that her husband's low-key lifestyle has made household chores much easier, particularly in the kitchen.
She admitted that while she initially expected to prepare heavy breakfasts like nasi lemak, Syed Saddiq actually prefers lighter options like Nestum during the week and pancakes at the weekend.
Despite their newfound domestic bliss, both affirmed that their careers remain firmly on track.
Syed Sadiq has returned to his parliamentary duties, while Bella continues to fulfill her singing and entertainment engagements.

At the heart of their new life is the well-being of Ayden and Ara. Bella shared a touching moment from their reception when her eldest son, Ayden, gave a speech with impressive confidence in front of the guests.

"As a mother, my children's happiness is my main priority. I want Ayden to go to school with peace of mind because children's emotions are very fragile. I am deeply grateful to see him speak so confidently while looking at me and his daddy. In many of our past videos, he would often cry, so seeing him so genuinely happy makes me feel extremely thankful," she said.

Syed Saddiq described Ayden's speech as one of the highlights of the evening, admitting that no speech of his own could match the courage shown by the nine-year-old. He also praised Bella for raising such well-mannered children.
As for a honeymoon, the couple have put plans on hold due to Syed Saddiq's parliamentary commitments, which run until December.

Joking that his immediate "destination" is Parliament, the politician revealed that long trips will have to wait until the session ends. In the meantime, they intend to make the most of short weekend getaways with the children.
"People often imagine that a honeymoon needs to be somewhere far away or atmospheric. But it really isn't about the location," Syed Saddiq said.
"If you are with the right person, anywhere can be the best honeymoon spot. I have the best partner and two wonderful kids. Wherever we go, it will surely be a cherished memory."
15bdb4c2078f404b: The wayward prince and his wife seem to be aiming for a reboot – searching for purpose, but not self-awareness Years ago, I was in Washington DC when Prince Harry blew through on an official engagement.
