f0aa4dd4a04596f8: KUALA LUMPUR DPMM and Johor Darul Ta'zim (JDT) will write an unprecedented chapter in FA Cup history on Friday at the Hassanal Bolkiah National Stadium, meeting in the competition's semi-final for the first time.
DPMM are Brunei FA Cup winners in 2004 and 2022 but they never reached the semi-finals until this campaign in the Malaysian FA Cup.

JDT enter the tie as five-time FA Cup champions (2016, 2022, 2023, 2024-2025, and 2025-2026), standing alone in Malaysian football history as the only club to lift the trophy four consecutive seasons - an era of knockout dominance crowned last December with a 5–0 demolition of Sabah in Bukit Jalil.

Since DPMM's return to the Super League, JDT have asserted complete authority, including a 3–0 win in their most recent meeting that has anchored the Southern Tigers' four-year domestic unbeaten streak.

For DPMM head coach Jamie McAllister, overcoming that psychological barrier in a two-legged knockout contest requires treating the home leg not as an all-or-nothing gamble, but as an exercise in structural discipline and game management.
"Top team. I mean, they're unbeaten in the last four years in the league," McAllister said.

"It's the first leg of the semi-final, we're at home, so hopefully there'll be a big crowd. We've just got to tighten up on a few little things defensively, especially against the top team in the league.
"If we do that, have that clean sheet mentality, and try and stay in the tie until the second leg, and see what happens."
However, JDT head coach Xisco Munoz has approached the trip across the South China Sea with total wariness, refusing to allow historical pedigree to lead to complacency.

JDT's tactical machine, which has plundered 28 goals without reply in the league this season, will need to remain balanced in transition against a DPMM side eager to sit deep, invite pressure, and counter vertically.
"We know it is a difficult team again. Always when we play away, they are a team that has balance," Munoz said.
"Sometimes when they play against us, they come in and stay in a low block, and they are stronger in this situation.
"It's not easy like this, and after, they have a good transition. We need to try to put the focus and give the best.
"We will try to have some rotation for the next game, but we need to try to choose the best one because it's difficult to take one step forward.
"These are the values of JDT. We don't need only 11 players, we need 20 players. Those who come in need to give more than those who played before."
a026d1bf840b300f: KUALA LUMPUR: Motorists in Malaysia have more than 10 navigation applications to choose from as alternatives to Waze, including Citymapper and GrabMaps.

Road Safety Experts Association (RSEA) founder Jamil Manan Supri said other options included Google Maps, PINTAZ, HERE WeGo, Apple Maps, TomTom, Sygic GPS Navigation, OsmAnd, Petal Maps, Moovit and Organic Maps.
However, he said switching from Waze to alternative applications should be accompanied by technical and safety assessments to ensure the reliability of route information and the safety of road users.
"Waze has an advantage through community reports on traffic congestion, accidents and road hazards, but the information provided is not necessarily complete, accurate or up to date.
"Technology should help reduce risks, not create new dependencies that could increase them," he said when contacted.

Commenting on the shift towards locally developed alternatives such as TuJu and PINTAZ, Jamil said the applications should be given opportunities to be evaluated and improved based on their actual performance, rather than simply because they were developed in Malaysia.
He said assessments should cover location accuracy, real-time traffic information, route suitability, system reliability and ease of use.
"Being a locally developed application does not, in itself, prove that it is safer, more accurate or offers better protection," he said.
On cybersecurity and road safety, Jamil said the two issues should be assessed separately, although they were interconnected.
He said concerns over the collection and processing of location data should be addressed through clear privacy policies, while allegations of data misuse must be supported by evidence.

"Application developers should explain what types of data are collected, the purposes for which they are used, how long they are stored, third-party access and the protective measures in place," he said.
Yesterday, the government announced a ban on the use of Waze among civil servants to protect government information and users' personal data from potential misuse by the Israeli regime.
In a statement, the Prime Minister's Office said the decision took into account the status of Waze Mobile Ltd as a data controller incorporated and operating under Israeli law.
It said the government remained firm in its position and would close any avenue that could be exploited by the Israeli regime to threaten national security and the public.

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was also reported yesterday as encouraging the public to use the locally developed TuJu application, developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority, as an alternative for road navigation.
a9f60b9db2fecd45: AFTER months of fires in Indonesia that have caused thick regional haze, attention is turning to whether companies can be held accountable for the blazes and resulting air pollution.

Indonesia experiences fires regularly during its dry season, and experts say years of deforestation and the draining of peatland for cultivation have rendered previously fire-resistant landscapes vulnerable.

Driven by a strong El Nino cycle and resulting drought, this year's blazes have been particularly severe, burning through nearly two million hectares, according to deforestation monitor Nusantara Atlas.
The fires have raged across forests and peatland but also palm oil and timber plantations supplying multinational firms.
Civil society groups have regularly accused companies of responsibility for the blazes, pointing to so-called "hotspots" in supplier plantations, sometimes called concessions.
Environmental group WALHI says it mapped "high confidence" hotspots across Indonesia using NASA fire data and found around 50 percent were inside concessions.
In a report this month the group listed 40 timber and palm oil concessions by the number of hotspots detected.
"This is a structural issue... (that) happens because of the practices, the activities, of these companies," WALHI forests and plantations campaigner Umi Ma'rufah told AFP.
Pressure is also coming from governments, including Singapore, which has issued 10 companies with "preventative measure notices" under its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act.
The notices urge them to fight fires on their land, prevent burning and submit action plans. Firms can face legal action including fines if they do not comply.
"We must also be clear about where the responsibility for this lies," Singapore Senior Minister K. Shanmugam told reporters.
"This was not simply an act of nature, but a problem driven by companies pursuing profits."
Several companies implicated have insisted they are not behind the fires.

"Fires originating outside our boundaries subsequently spread into areas under the Group's management," Singapore Exchange-listed palm oil company First Resources said after one of its concessions was listed in WALHI's report.

Asia Pulp and Paper, a Singapore-registered firm, also insisted that fires in supplier concessions do not "necessarily mean that land was deliberately burned or that the concession holder was responsible for starting the fire."
Satellite monitoring can sometimes show where fires started, said Nusantara Atlas founder David Gaveau.
"In some cases, the satellite photos clearly show that fire starts inside, but we cannot say whether it's by design or whether it's accidental," he told AFP.
"In other cases it's also clear that fire started outside and spread inside the concession."
Experts say fire has been used in the past to illegally open up land for cultivation, including in large concessions, but also by smaller-scale local investors.
Parts of Indonesia also previously allowed smallholders to use fire to clear plots of land, though this year the government has cracked down on that practice too.
Even if fires begin accidentally or outside concessions, firms may have legal responsibilities, explained Azam Hawari, a lawyer with environmental law NGO ClientEarth.
"An external source of ignition or extreme weather does not necessarily absolve a company of civil liability," said Hawari.

Companies are required to have sufficient fire measures, including personnel and equipment, and could also be liable "where activities pose a serious threat to the environment," like peatland drainage, he added.
Indonesia has announced "administrative sanctions" against dozens of firms and criminal proceedings against 125 individuals and corporations.
But campaigner Umi pointed out that some previously prosecuted firms have failed to pay fines or carry out forest restoration.
"It's about the will from the government to really do their (enforcement) task," she said.
Some implicated concessions have ties well behind Indonesia's borders, said Holly Yang, an accounting professor at Singapore Management University who teaches sustainability reporting.
After WALHI's report, she and her student Ashmit Bansal mapped concession holders, owners, creditors, investors and supply-chain partners.
"The fires occur in Indonesia, but the ownership, financing and commercial relationships extend across borders," Yang told AFP.
Yang noted that a connection "does not, by itself, establish responsibility for a fire."
But mapping relationships "allows the public to ask informed questions and assess how those parties respond."

3879af4ad42575d3: PETALING JAYA: Kampung Tunku assemblyman Lim Yi Wei today urged Malaysians to stop sharing videos of incidents of violence in schools on social media, calling on the media to avoid sensationalising such incidents as well.

The DAP assemblyman said her call was to prevent social contagion, a psychological phenomenon in which behaviours, emotions or ideas spread quickly and spontaneously, potentially triggering copycat incidents.
"Having physical and online discussions and sharing information feels helpful, but where do we draw the line between solidarity and sensationalism?" she said in a statement.
Sarawak police previously said that a teenager who allegedly attacked a teacher at Tunku Putra-HELP International School in Kuching yesterday morning had live-streamed the incident.

State acting police commissioner Saifullizan Ishak said the recording, lasting 12 minutes and six seconds, showed the attack from the teenager’s perspective and was taken down by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.
Lim expressed disappointment over social media posts on the Kuching incident that used the hashtags "#viralkan" and "#fyp" to boost their visibility.
"They exploit legitimate shock and concerns about school safety, which generates likes, shares and sometimes income for the poster," she said.

Lim said a 2015 US study found that mass killings involving firearms, including school shootings, were motivated by similar events in the immediate past, with the temporary increase in probability lasting an average of 13 days.

"Outside this period, perpetrators of particularly horrific massacres such as those at Virginia Tech, Sandy Hook and Umpqua Community College, clearly cited mass killers before them as inspiration for their attacks," she said.

Lim said discussions on school violence should not involve sharing videos or sensationalising attackers' actions and manifestos, but that social media platforms had little incentive to remove such content because their business models thrived on heated discourse and virality.
"We say children are susceptible to the influence of social media; (the theory of) social contagion explains that adults are not immune.
"We must confront ourselves: are we sharing because we really care, or because our brains thrive on the endorphin rush from online validation?" she said.
1a94692dc4a73ccb: NIBONG TEBAL: The Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry seized 6.4 tonnes of cooking oil worth RM20,166 and detained three men, including two foreigners, during a raid on an unnumbered storage facility in Kampung Sanglang yesterday.

The operation was conducted with the marine police after enforcement officers uncovered about 900kg of one-kilogramme cooking oil packets, 4,000 cut-open packets and an estimated 5,500kg of cooking oil stored in six intermediate bulk container (IBC) tanks.
Other items seized included a pump motor, hoses and an aluminium storage tank.
State Domestic Trade and Cost of Living director S. Jegan said the three suspects would be remanded to assist in investigations.

"The case is being investigated under Section 21 of the Control of Supplies Act 1961 and Regulation 3(1) of the Control of Supplies Regulations 1974," he said in a statement, adding that an investigation paper had been opened.
The seizure followed a similar integrated operation by the ministry and the northern region marine police at a premises in Penaga on Oct 12.
That operation uncovered the suspected transfer of packaged cooking oil into storage tanks, with seizures valued at RM65,450.
Jegan said any direct link between the two cases would depend on the outcome of investigations.
He said the ministry would intensify enforcement to curb the suspected misuse of subsidised cooking oil, which is intended for eligible Malaysians.

Members of the public with information on the misuse of controlled goods can lodge complaints via the ministry's WhatsApp hotline at 019-848 8000, its e-Aduan portal at eaduan.kpdn.gov.my, the toll-free hotline at 1-800-886-800 or the EzADU mobile application.

ff98a9e4102ca0eb: MADRID: Europe's richest football clubs have built a commercial engine that generates almost half their income, helping underpin an expanding financial elite whose membership has proved harder to change than its revenues, a study shows.

The report by consultancy Football Benchmark and World Football Summit charts two transformations: commercial income has displaced broadcasting as the leading revenue source for the highest earners, while growth across European football has failed to narrow the financial divide.

Commercial and other income accounted for 49% of operating revenue at the 10 highest-earning clubs in 2024/25, compared with 32% in 2008/09. Broadcasting, including UEFA distributions, fell from 42% to 32%, and stadium and matchday income from 27% to 19%.

Those are declining shares of a much larger business, not evidence of falling receipts. The top 10's combined operating revenue more than tripled over those 16 years, from 2.7 billion euros to 8.4 billion.
The shift came in two stages.

Commercial income overtook broadcasting in the early 2010s. Up to 2018/19, its gains came largely at the expense of matchday income, whose share fell to 16%, while broadcasting’s slipped only to 40%. The report says that phase coincided with the digitalisation and internationalisation of football through social media and new digital platforms.

Since the pandemic, broadcasting has given ground instead, its share falling from 38% in 2021/22 to 32% in 2024/25, while matchday income has recovered. The commercial category includes other income and should not be read as sponsorship alone.
Growth without convergence
The study draws on UEFA financial reports, Deloitte's Football Money League and Football Benchmark's own data.
Football Benchmark provides consultancy services and data analysis to clubs, leagues, governing bodies and investors on the business of football.
World Football Summit organises industry events and initiatives that bring football executives and other businesses together to develop partnerships and commercial opportunities.

Across Europe's 700 top-division clubs, operating revenue increased from 11.6 billion euros in 2008/09 to 28.6 billion in 2023/24. The report estimates it exceeded 30 billion for the first time in 2024/25.

More clubs have crossed previously exceptional revenue thresholds. Thirty-three generated over 200 million euros in 2024/25, against eight in 2008/09, while the number exceeding 300 million rose from three to 17.
The distribution has shifted towards England. Premier League clubs generated 26% of European top-flight revenue in 2023/24, up from 21% in 2008/09.
Six English clubs featured among the top 10 earners in 2024/25, compared with four at the start of the period. Italy went from three representatives to none.
The report says the biggest clubs have widened their financial advantage over the rest in absolute terms, even as the wider industry has grown.
“The growth is not homogeneous. The richest clubs become richer at a faster pace than the others,” Antonio Di Cianni, Football Benchmark’s director of advisory, told Reuters.
“Thanks to their global fan base, these clubs have become media powerhouses. Nowadays, we couldn’t consider them simple football clubs anymore.”

Di Cianni also points to the new format of the Champions League, which grew the most in revenue among UEFA’s club competitions, deepening that concentration because the biggest domestic clubs were more likely to take part.

“It becomes a virtuous or vicious cycle depending on the perspective. The higher revenues these clubs generate, the better squads they are able to assemble, the better results on the pitch they get,” he said.
Television still counts

Commercial and other revenue was also the fastest-growing main income stream across European top-flight football between 2014/15 and 2023/24, increasing at a compound annual rate of 7% to 12.6 billion euros.
Multi-year agreements helped make it the most resilient stream during the pandemic, the report said.

Broadcasting nevertheless remains particularly important for smaller and mid-sized clubs. Domestic broadcasting receipts rose from 5.8 billion euros to 8.5 billion over that period, while Uefa distributions roughly doubled to 3.2 billion.
Matchday revenue recovered from 500 million euros in 2020/21 to 4.4 billion in 2023/24, surpassing pre-pandemic levels.
Rising income has accompanied record valuations, but little turnover at the top.
Football Benchmark put the combined enterprise value of Europe's 32 most valuable clubs at 72.6 billion euros in 2026, nearly three times the 2016 figure.
Only 11 clubs appeared among the 10 most valuable over that decade — a measure of how durable football's financial hierarchy has become despite the scale of its expansion.
f76fd8e1b9026e11: KUALA LUMPUR: The implementation of the Budi Madani Diesel (Budi Diesel) has successfully curbed fuel leakage compared with the previous mechanism.

Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said this was reflected in a 10 per cent decline in diesel consumption in Sabah last month, despite recipients in the region being given an additional monthly quota of 100 litres.
He said the decline was among the indications that the targeted subsidy mechanism could curb leakage, while ensuring that the public continued to have access to diesel and RON95 at subsidised prices.

"Whether it helps to increase productivity is a separate question. However, the government wants to ensure that there is no fuel leakage, so that the public can continue to enjoy supplies at lower prices," he said in Dewan Rakyat today.

He was responding to a supplementary question from Salamiah Mohd Nor (PN-Temerloh) on the assessment of the effectiveness of targeted fuel subsidies and whether the policy had helped improve productivity, particularly for industrial players.

Meanwhile, in reply to the initial question, Liew said additional eligibility under Budi Diesel was introduced after the government took into account the widespread use of pickup trucks and jeeps as primary vehicles, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak, where many residents rely on these vehicles for their daily activities.
As of Oct 12, a total of 52,133 diesel pickup truck and jeep owners in Sabah had qualified for the extra 100 litres a month under the scheme.
He said the government also improved the Budi Diesel mechanism from Sept 16 by allowing eligibility to be transferred to the actual users of diesel vehicles.
"Eligible registered owners can now transfer their eligibility to any Malaysian citizen with a valid MyKad who qualifies for BUDI95 and is the actual user of the vehicle.

"For individuals who own more than one private diesel vehicle, eligibility can also be transferred to a maximum of three other people, subject to the number of diesel vehicles owned and eligibility checks.
Eligible registered owners of pickup trucks and jeeps may also apply for the additional 100-litre allocation before transferring their entitlement, subject to the scheme's conditions.
As of Oct 12, the government had approved 19,008 applications to transfer Budi Diesel eligibility, of which 5,555 were from Sabah, he said.
Liew said the government would continue assessing the scheme using diesel consumption data, public feedback, input from state governments and the requirements of the sectors involved.

"Any further improvements will be evaluated based on data to ensure subsidies reach eligible users through a more accessible, fair, targeted and sustainable mechanism, while preventing leakage and abuse," he said.
3e30b1b2270e5310: WASHINGTON: The US agriculture department (USDA) said on Wednesday it confirmed the first detection of flesh-eating parasite New World screwworm in US wildlife in an elk in Pecos County, Texas, while New Mexico authorities separately said they confirmed a case in a beef cow.
The elk was located on a game ranch and was reported after being harvested by a hunter, the USDA said in a statement.

"The Texas Animal Health Commission will modify a previously established infested zone, and the USDA and the Texas Parks and Wildlife Department are conducting additional wildlife surveillance in the area," the USDA said.
The New Mexico Department of Agriculture said later that animal health officials confirmed a case of New World screwworm in a beef cow in the state's Otero County.

New Mexico authorities said state and federal officials were continuing to expand surveillance and fly-trapping around affected locations to identify any additional cases and determine whether the pest had spread beyond the affected animals.
"Officials have established a minimum 20km radius infested zone around the affected animal's location," the New Mexico Department of Agriculture said.
"Within this zone, animals must be inspected and, if necessary, treated before moving within or out of the area," state authorities added.
Eradicated from the US decades ago, the pest has surged north from Central America through Mexico, prompting Washington to impose a more than year-long ban on Mexican cattle imports.
The US halted livestock imports from Mexico last year to keep out screwworm but resumed trade in August at an Arizona port as part of a phased reopening plan.
The halt tightened US cattle supplies, contributing to a rise in beef prices to record highs for American consumers.
b81b02fbb1e375d6: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Malaysia could generate new sources of revenue by developing its marine-fuel industry and positioning itself as a regional hub for blending, storing and supplying fuel to ships, said maritime industry expert Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan.

Jeyenderan, who has more than 30 years of experience in the maritime and shipping industry, said Malaysia should make better use of its petroleum resources, palm oil industry, storage facilities and ports to generate greater economic value locally.

His proposal follows a call by Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari for the government to broaden its revenue base and identify new strategic industries that could generate sustainable returns for the country.

Amirudin, who is also the Pakatan Harapan (PH) MP for Gombak, said government commitments, including subsidies, civil service emoluments, debt servicing and retirement benefits, constrained its ability to fund development and economic transformation.

He also urged the Finance Ministry to explain how economic growth, investment and trade could translate into higher government revenue, and proposed greater diversification to reduce reliance on income from Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) and government-linked investment companies.

Responding to the issue, Jeyenderan said developing Malaysia into a regional marine-fuel hub could create new business opportunities while allowing the country to capture more value from its existing petroleum resources.
He identified very low sulphur fuel oil (VLSFO), a type of marine fuel used by ships, as one area Malaysia could explore to strengthen its position in the international shipping industry.

Ships use VLSFO to comply with the International Maritime Organization’s global sulphur limit, which generally restricts the sulphur content of fuel oil used on board vessels to 0.50 per cent. The limit, which came into force in January 2020, has created demand for marine fuels that meet the required specifications.
Jeyenderan said Malaysia could explore producing VLSFO by blending suitable petroleum products, storing the finished fuel and supplying it to vessels passing through the region.
This, he said, would allow local companies to participate in more stages of the marine-fuel supply chain instead of focusing mainly on transporting petroleum cargo.

“For example, a company could obtain suitable fuel components from refineries or petroleum suppliers, blend them in controlled proportions and test the resulting product to ensure it meets the required sulphur limit and other fuel specifications.
“The finished VLSFO could then be stored in dedicated tanks before being delivered to ships at ports or through bunker vessels.

“Another opportunity would be to receive different petroleum products at Malaysian storage terminals, combine suitable components to produce fuel that meets a buyer’s requirements, and sell the finished product to shipping operators.
“Such operations would require appropriate equipment, quality testing and documentation to ensure the fuel meets specifications and remains suitable for use.

“We could make more money from oil cargo by doing more of the work locally, including mixing the fuel, storing it and selling it to ships, instead of simply receiving and moving the cargo,” he said in a statement.
He said a regional marine-fuel hub could create opportunities across fuel blending, storage, trading, transportation and bunkering, which involves supplying fuel to vessels.
“These activities could support local businesses and generate additional demand for port services, logistics and petroleum trading,” he said.

However, Jeyenderan said Malaysia would need clear regulatory and operational guidelines to support the industry’s development, particularly in the handling, storage, transfer and blending of petroleum products.
He added that proper documentation and transparent procedures would help protect government revenue, give businesses greater certainty and encourage investment in higher-value activities.
By developing its marine-fuel capabilities, he said, Malaysia could tap an additional source of economic activity while strengthening its position in the regional maritime and energy supply chain.
e5dbc0be8d9e7187: PETALING JAYA: Pakatan Harapan (PH) mungkin bertanding maksimum 21 daripada 28 DUN Melaka mengambil kira aspek jentera, keupayaan calon, dan penerimaan pengundi.
Pengerusi PH Melaka Adly Zahari, berkata namun perkara itu hanya akan dimuktamadkan melalui mesyuarat Majlis Presiden PH esok, sebelum diumumkan Sabtu ini.

"Saya tak fikir PH akan bertanding semua kerusi. Daripada awal kita sudah tahu kita tidak akan bertanding 28 kerusi, sebaliknya memberi tumpuan pada kerusi yang kita ada kekuatan berdasarkan tiga faktor tadi.

"Kita rasa strategi itu lebih baik...kalau kita lihat di Johor dan Negeri Sembilan, kita bertanding solo pada keseluruhan kerusi, namun di Melaka kita ambil langkah strategik," katanya menurut Berita Harian.
Adly yang juga bekas ketua menteri Melaka, berkata PH mempunyai peluang menang lebih baik apabila menumpukan kepada kerusi berpotensi.
Menjawab dakwaan PH memberi laluan kepada Bersatu, Adly berkata, ketika ini PH fokus menghadapi PRN secara bersendiri.
Katanya, tiada rundingan dibuat di peringkat negeri berhubung kerjasama itu, sebaliknya hanya membabitkan kerusi akan ditandingi PH.
"Selalunya orang akan melihat kalau ada kerjasama politik, tiada pertembungan...namun fokus kita adalah bagaimana kita boleh memberikan tumpuan pada kerusi yang ingin ditandingi."
PRN Melaka akan berlangsung 14 Nov dengan penamaan calon ditetapkan 31 Okt.
8e73b460bc754331: JAKARTA: Polis Indonesia menamakan 11 syarikat sebagai suspek dalam siasatan berterusan terhadap kebakaran hutan dan tanah termasuk tiga daripadanya firma pelaburan asing, menurut agensi berita negara Antara.
Ketua Polis Indonesia, Suyudi Ario Set enggan mengumumkan nama syarikat-syarikat berkenaan tetapi berkata siasatan diteruskan tanpa halangan besar.
Beliau memberitahu pemberita selepas mesyuarat Kabinet pleno di kompleks Istana Presiden di Jakarta pada Rabu bahawa akauntabiliti akan mengatasi entiti korporat berkenaan.
"Ini termasuk kedua-dua pemilik syarikat dan pemegang saham yang bertanggungjawab ke atas perbadanan yang dikaitkan dengan kebakaran hutan dan tanah di Indonesia," kata Suyudi.

Menurut laporan itu, prosiding jenayah berkenaan adalah susulan pengumuman awal oleh Agensi Siasatan Jenayah Polis Negara (Bareskrim) yang mengatakan ia telah memajukan 98 laporan polis berhubung kebakaran hutan berkaitan korporat ke peringkat siasatan rasmi.
Di samping siasatan polis, Kementerian Perhutanan turut meningkatkan penguatkuasaan pentadbiran.

Menteri Perhutanan Raja Juli Antoni berkata permit untuk enam lagi syarikat di Kalimantan Tengah telah digantung, menjadikan jumlah keseluruhan firma perhutanan yang dibenarkan kepada 32, menurut laporan itu.
Keenam-enam syarikat tersebut telah digantung Permit Perniagaan Penggunaan Hutan (PBPH) dan diarah menjalankan pemulihan alam sekitar di kawasan terjejas.
Mereka ialah PT Produk Kalimantan Jaya, PT Taiyong Engreen, PT Hutan Produk Lestari, PT Ramang Agro Lestari, PT Puspa Warna Cemerlang dan PT Sinergi Hutan Sejati.
Enam syarikat itu memegang konsesi seluas 201,391 hektar, di mana 7,531 hektar daripadanya terjejas akibat kebakaran baru-baru ini.
Sekatan pentadbiran kementerian itu kini meliputi 32 syarikat yang menguruskan lebih 1.9 juta hektar konsesi, termasuk 18,489 hektar yang terjejas akibat kebakaran.
Raja Juli memberi amaran bahawa syarikat itu juga boleh berdepan prosiding jenayah yang berasingan jika penyiasatan menemukan bukti salah laku yang disengajakan atau niat jenayah.
d1675265f6fc0891: IPOH: A 49-year-old lorry workshop owner has claimed trial at the Sessions Court here to eight charges of failing to pay goods and services tax (GST) and penalties totalling RM271,875.
Look Pek Kong entered the plea after the charges under Section 41(7) of the Goods and Services Tax Act were read out before Judge Ainul Shahrin Mohamad today.
According to the charges, Look failed to pay GST for eight taxable periods between April 1, 2016 and June 30, 2018. The offences were committed at the Perak Customs Department.
The outstanding GST amounted to RM226,040, while the penalties totalled RM45,835.
If convicted, Look faces a fine of up to RM50,000, imprisonment for up to three years, or both, for each offence.
He also faces two other charges under Section 165(4) of the same Act and Section 57(4) of the Service Tax Act for allegedly failing to produce documents requested by Customs officers.
Customs Department prosecuting officers Nur Amalina Ahmad Nazeri and Ar Junadi Jamaluddin prosecuted, while Look was unrepresented.
The prosecution proposed bail of RM3,000 for each charge, but Look appealed for a lower amount, saying he could only afford RM1,000 per charge.
The court set bail at RM1,000 for each of the eight charges, with one surety, bringing the total to RM8,000.
The court fixed Nov 19 for mention.
The prosecution said Look was expected to pay the bail later today.
3cf55decbd424670: Indian certification authority eMudhra has defended the laughably weak private keys it used to sign some digital certificates it issued, and suggested others should share the blame for the incident.

In case you’re coming to this one late, news broke yesterday that private keys the company used to sign certs were beyond weak: one was literally just the number “4,” and several others were short strings of easily guessed two-or-three-digit numbers. It’s easy to deduce the value of those keys, which makes it possible to forge certs and impersonate websites or other resources.

That’s gold for scammers, phishers, and other miscreants. The entire infosec industry has pointed that out, urged swift adoption of better certs, and lamented the fact that implementing replacements will be a long and thankless task.
eMudhra’s statement about the incident says it generated keys during “a Key Generation Ceremony (KGC) held on April 30, 2025, using FIPS 140-2 Level 3 Hardware Security Modules (HSMs).”
Such hardware is the standard kit for the job and should in theory produce nicely complex keys and store them securely.

“A flaw in the KGC caused a wrap/unwrap step to produce a second set of weak keys alongside the original strong keys,” the statement claims. “The weak keys were the ones published to the browser root stores. eMudhra is working to establish the root cause.”
The company then gets a tad defensive.

“These roots and issuing CAs have gone through independent audits for two years in a row and have been in browser trust lists since mid-2025,” the statement adds, seemingly shifting some blame to auditors and other stakeholders.
The announcement then points out that eMudhra’s TLS business generates just one percent of its revenue, meaning this mess won’t impact its bottom line too much.
That’s nice to know for the company’s investors but rather misses the point that whoever relies on the company now has an urgent, unwanted, and costly job to do replacing certs.

“eMudhra is working directly with customers who may be affected to give them replacement certificates, so that critical services are not disrupted. The company is also working with the root programs and continues its root-cause investigation,” the statement adds.
The company allows that the incident “may have some reputational risks on eMudhra which cannot be quantified.”
cf52b393e0d29909: JAKARTA: Indonesian police have named 11 corporations as suspects in ongoing investigations into forest and land fires, three of which are foreign-invested firms, according to state news agency Antara.
National Police Chief General Suyudi Ario Seto declined to name the companies but said the investigations were proceeding without major obstacles.
He told reporters after a plenary Cabinet meeting at the Presidential Palace complex in Jakarta on Wednesday that accountability would extend beyond the corporate entities themselves.
"This includes both company owners and shareholders who bear responsibility for the corporations linked to forest and land fires in Indonesia," Suyudi said.

The report said the investigations followed an earlier announcement by the National Police's Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim) that it had elevated 98 police reports concerning forest fires linked to corporations to the formal investigation stage.
Alongside the police investigations, the Forestry Ministry has stepped up administrative enforcement.
Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni said permits for six more companies in Central Kalimantan had been suspended, bringing the total number of forestry firms sanctioned to 32, according to the report.
The six companies had their Forest Utilisation Business Permits (PBPH) suspended and were ordered to undertake environmental restoration in affected areas.
They are PT Produk Kalimantan Jaya, PT Taiyong Engreen, PT Hutan Produk Lestari, PT Ramang Agro Lestari, PT Puspa Warna Cemerlang and PT Sinergi Hutan Sejati.
Together, the six companies hold concessions covering 201,391 hectares, of which 7,531 hectares were affected by recent fires.
The ministry's administrative sanctions now cover 32 companies managing more than 1.9 million hectares of concessions, including 18,489 hectares affected by fires.
Raja Juli warned that the companies could also face separate criminal proceedings if investigations uncovered evidence of deliberate wrongdoing or criminal intent.
9def48c554c457d0: CYBERJAYA: The e-wallet function in the TuJu navigation app is a planned feature that has yet to be developed, the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) said.
MHA operations and maintenance director Mohd Shahrir Amin Ahmad said TuJu was originally conceived as a "super app", but the current focus was on navigation.
"The e-wallet is meant for when we are on a journey and stop at a rest and service area.
"It is a future feature that has yet to be built into the app. It is still in the planning stage.
"Right now, we are focusing on navigation and our highway features," he told a press conference here today.
He was responding to a question on why TuJu collects financial data, such as e-wallet transactions, unlike Waze.
Shahrir said TuJu 2.0 upgraded existing features, including navigation, CCTV footage and traffic information on accidents, while adding electric vehicle (EV) charging stations and local attractions.
"We also have features similar to Google's, where users can set fixed destinations they frequently visit.
"Users can also locate where their car is parked, for example, in a large parking area.
"We have added many features in version 2. It has been launched on Android, while the iOS version is expected by the end of this month.
"This is because Apple is still testing version 2 before releasing it on the App Store," he said.

MHA deputy director-general (operations) Ir Dr Mohammed Ridzuan Jahidin said the app also had an SOS button that sends emergency information to the relevant highway concessionaire if users encounter problems on the highway.
"Downloads have now exceeded 700,000 since yesterday, and we are improving our services, especially navigation. The other features can still be used," he said.
a0a10bc52c403d7a: GUA MUSANG, Oct 22 — The Public Works Department (JKR) in Kelantan has confirmed a landslide along Jalan Lojing-Gua Musang (FT185), near Yayasan Albarakah here yesterday, which caused a 30-metre-long crack in the road surface.
Kelantan JKR director Nik Badlihisham Nik Ismail said the landslide at Section 84.15 involved an area stretching 20 metres in length and 30 metres in depth.
He said monitoring was being carried out at the site, while warning signs had been installed to alert road users to the danger.
“Damage was also detected to the slope drainage system.
“However, the road remains open to all vehicles, and no alternative route has been provided so far,” he told Bernama today.
Meanwhile, Gua Musang police chief Supt Sik Choon Foo said no casualties had been reported in the incident.

He advised motorists to observe warning signs and exercise caution when passing through the area, especially during rain, and not to proceed if cracks appeared on the road, as the ground might be unstable. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: JKR stands for Jabatan Kerja Raya, or the Public Works Department. Supt is short for Superintendent.
99f39b315ee72158: PETALING JAYA: Prosedur operasi standard (SOP) keselamatan sahaja tidak cukup untuk membendung keganasan di sekolah tanpa langkah pencegahan, latihan guru dan sokongan kaunselor.

Setiausaha Agung Kesatuan Perkhidmatan Perguruan Kebangsaan (NUTP), Fouzi Singon, berkata pendekatan keselamatan perlu beralih daripada tindakan selepas kejadian kepada usaha mencegah keganasan daripada berlaku.
“Kita hendak pencegahan. Orang bicarakan tentang semua benda yang dah berlaku. Kita tak kehendak yang berlaku. Kita nak mencegah daripada berlaku,” katanya kepada FMT.

Semalam, Ahli Parlimen Kuching Bandar Baru, Dr Kelvin Yii, meminta SOP keselamatan sekolah dikaji semula susulan kejadian seorang pelajar lelaki berusia 16 tahun disyaki menyerang guru wanita menggunakan objek dipercayai kapak di sebuah sekolah antarabangsa di Kuching.
Kelvin turut mempersoalkan langkah kerajaan menyediakan sokongan kesihatan mental kepada mangsa dan pelajar terbabit, selain menggesa penelitian terhadap pengaruh media sosial serta permainan video.

Sementara itu, Fouzi berkata guru disiplin dan kaunselor memerlukan latihan khusus untuk mengendalikan kes buli, pemerasan dan konflik pelajar termasuk menjalankan siasatan serta menentukan tindakan susulan.
Beliau turut mempersoalkan keberkesanan langkah terlalu tertumpu pada kemudahan fizikal seperti kamera litar tertutup (CCTV), yang lebih membantu merekod kejadian berbanding mencegahnya.

Pengerusi Pertubuhan Ikatan Komuniti Selamat (Ikatan), Lee Lam Thye, pula berkata usaha membendung keganasan perlu meneliti puncanya termasuk kemungkinan masalah kesihatan mental dan tekanan dialami pelajar.
“Saya rasa kes berlaku di sekolah memang ada kaitan dengan isu kesihatan mental. Sejauh mana program-program untuk menangani isu kesihatan mental dan tekanan dialami pelajar? soalnya.
Katanya, usaha meningkatkan keselamatan tidak boleh bergantung pada guru semata-mata kerana mereka turut mempunyai tanggungjawab mengajar.
“Sekolah juga memerlukan sokongan kaunselor yang mencukupi untuk menangani masalah emosi dan tingkah laku pelajar.
“Kita juga nak tanya ibu bapa apa tanggungjawab mereka dalam mendidik anak-anak supaya apabila bersekolah, anak-anak berdisiplin dan mematuhi peraturan,” katanya.
Menurutnya, guru perlu dilatih mengenal pasti pelajar yang memerlukan bantuan dan merujuk mereka kepada kaunselor, dengan pencegahan memerlukan kerjasama sekolah, keluarga dan masyarakat.
dc516ad350a72608: SUNGAI PETANI: Nine men were charged in the sessions court here today with being members of an organised crime group known as Geng Suria.
The nine are Thayalan, 28; A Tana Balan, 30; Rizwan Abd Jalil, 28; G Sritharan, 39; B Saranraj, 38; A Simon, 34; G Suria Prasad (alleged to be the gang leader), 30; A Suresh, 52; and Kavines, 31.
No pleas were recorded after the charges were read out in Tamil before judges Nabisha Ibrahim and Najwa Che Mat in separate courtrooms, as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
The nine men are charged with being members of an organised crime group at an unnumbered house on Jalan Sekerat, Pekan Lama, here, between December 2024 and April this year.
The charge, framed under Section 130V(1) of the Penal Code, provides for imprisonment of up to 20 years upon conviction.
The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutors Yazid Mustaqim Roslan and Fakhrurrazi Ahmad Salim.
Lawyer S Sagthiyaraj represented Saranraj and Thayalan, while lawyer Naim Kamaruddin represented Sritharan, Simon and Tana Balan. The remaining four accused were unrepresented.
The court denied bail to all nine and set Nov 17 for mention.
1083fc894c418e41: KUALA LUMPUR: The government is finalising the Natural Gas Roadmap (NGR) to guide the coordinated development of Malaysia's gas sector in line with national policies and the 13th Malaysia Plan, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir.

"I wish to thank all stakeholders who have contributed to this process. A roadmap will matter only if it translates into projects, reforms and measurable outcomes," he said in his pre-recorded video for the Malaysian Gas Symposium (MyGAS) 2026 today.
He said Malaysia must strengthen its gas supply resilience amid global market uncertainty and rising energy demand from advanced manufacturing, data centres and digital industries.

"We have seen how quickly global conditions can change. Disruptions to international liquefied natural gas (LNG) trade this year have affected availability and heightened price volatility across our region.

"The lesson is straightforward: Malaysia must not depend on favourable global market conditions. We must strengthen our own resilience -- through diversified supply, sound procurement, infrastructure readiness and effective market arrangements.

"This means supporting the development of domestic gas resources, diversifying sources of imported LNG to complement domestic supply, and ensuring that infrastructure is available to deliver gas to consumers," he said.

He said the development of domestic gas resources must account for the differing resource positions and development needs of Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak, in collaboration with the respective state governments and relevant industry players.

As a country that both produces and imports gas, he said Malaysia must also continue to strengthen relationships with supplying countries and regional partners, while maintaining its standing as a reliable participant in international gas trade.
Akmal Nasrullah said natural gas would remain important for electricity system flexibility, industrial production and high-value economic activities.

Under the National Energy Transition Roadmap's (NETR) Responsible Transition pathway, natural gas is projected to account for 56 per cent of Malaysia's total primary energy supply by 2050, supporting reliable electricity supply as renewable energy expands.
The government has agreed to the development of the Third Regasification Terminal (RGT3) in Lumut, Perak, to strengthen Malaysia's long-term gas supply security.

Targeted to commence commercial operations in the second quarter of 2029, RGT3 is expected to enhance the resilience and flexibility of the country's gas supply infrastructure, support growing domestic energy demand and reinforce investor confidence in Malaysia's energy security.
He said technologies such as carbon capture, utilisation and storage as well as biomethane offer further opportunities where they are technically suitable and commercially viable.

"I encourage the industry to demonstrate progress through measurable reductions in emissions. We must create more economic value from every unit of gas, while reducing its environmental footprint," he said.

Meanwhile, Ministry of Economy secretary-general Datuk Seri Nor Azmie Diron said the NGR aims to balance energy security, affordability and environmental sustainability, while also addressing the differing gas development needs in Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.

On new gas infrastructure for Peninsular Malaysia, he said the development of the regasification terminal in Lumut, Perak and Yan, Kedah will add more than 1,000 million standard cubic feet per day (MMscfd) of capacity, strengthening energy security, particularly across northern Peninsular Malaysia.

In Sabah, further investments will focus on developing virtual pipeline systems as well as exploring offshore gas sources on the East Coast and future regasification terminals, in line with the Sabah Energy Roadmap and Master Plan 2040.
"As for Sarawak, the NGR recognises the four gas hubs in Kuching, Bintulu, Samalaju and Miri that have been identified in the Sarawak Gas Roadmap," he said.
He said the roadmap would also improve gas market efficiency through third-party access and digital systems to facilitate gas trading and capacity booking.

Meanwhile, Malaysian Gas Association (MGA) president Abang Yusuf Abang Puteh said that amid growing global uncertainty and changing energy markets, the focus must now shift from identifying challenges to finding practical solutions that strengthen Malaysia's energy security, resilience and long-term competitiveness.
He said one key lesson from our experience is that every part of the energy system is interconnected, and our efforts must be equally collaborative.
"Gas supply must reach the people and industries that need it. Infrastructure must be reliable and ready for changing demand.
"Projects need investment, and investment depends on confidence. Each of us holds part of the solution; progress comes when we bring those parts together," he said.
MyGAS 2026 is a half-day event organised by MGA, with this year's theme, "Powering Confidence: Practical Pathways for a Resilient Energy Future".
