c201e3fca1cc5ae1: KUALA LUMPUR: Cheah Liek Hou showed his fighting spirit at the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, battling a hamstring injury sustained just a week before departure to secure a gold and bronze medal for Malaysia.
The two-time Paralympic champion settled for bronze in the men's singles SU5 event on Thursday after retiring midway through his semi-final against China's Li Ming Pan.
Liek Hou, 38, won the second game to level the tie but had to retire with a hamstring injury after trailing 11-7 in the decider at the Ichinomiya Municipal Gymnasium in Aichi.
His coach, Nova Armada, revealed that Liek Hou had suffered the hamstring injury just a week before leaving for Japan.
"He suffered a hamstring injury a week before we left for the Asian Para Games," said Nova when contacted.
"We didn't want the tear to extend to his tendon."
The injury meant Liek Hou had to manage his physical condition throughout the competition, with the risk of aggravating it remaining a concern.
Despite the setback, the Malaysian veteran pressed on and added two more medals to his collection.
He won his singles bronze after partnering Faris Ahmad Azri to capture the men's doubles SU5 gold medal on Wednesday.
The Malaysian pair defeated South Korea's Jeon Sunwoo-Kim Gi Yeon 21-8, 21-13 to end the country's 12-year wait for the title.
Liek Hou had previously won the singles gold at the 2010 Guangzhou and 2014 Incheon Games, making him one of Malaysia's most successful para badminton players.

Although his hopes of reclaiming the singles crown ended prematurely, Liek Hou will return home with another impressive medal haul, underlining his determination to deliver for Malaysia despite the injury setback.
39d331a49c8e0e4b: DUBAI: The IMF on Thursday forecast a sharp drop in economic output in the Middle East, North Africa and Pakistan this year due to the US-Israeli-led war against Iran, followed by a rebound to 6.6% growth in 2027, while warning that further energy production disruptions could worsen the outlook.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said the region's output was expected to contract by 1.3% as a result of the war's impact on energy production, shipping, tourism, trade and confidence. Economic output would increase sharply in 2027, but output in those economies would generally stay below pre-war projections.

The war's impact had been substantial, but uneven, with oil-exporting economies directly affected by disruptions to energy production and shipping hit harder, and oil importers proving to be more resilient, the IMF said in its regional outlook released Thursday in Dubai.

The IMF said its baseline assumed that the conflict would abate in early 2027 and that trade would gradually normalize during the year, but it said the outlook remained clouded by "exceptionally high uncertainty."

"The main risks derive from further disruption to energy production and trade routes that could drive energy prices higher," the IMF said in a statement outlining its key messages, noting external financial conditions could also tighten.

External financial conditions could also tighten if investors reassess AI-driven productivity gains and interest rates rise further amid heightened concerns about inflation and fiscal positions, it said.

Oil importers had proven more resilient, with domestic demand supported by remittances and tourism flows, favorable financial conditions, and prompt policy responses that safeguard consumers from higher commodity prices, the IMF said.
Growth in the Caucasus and Central Asia was moderating toward a more sustainable pace, the IMF said, forecasting a 5.2% rise in economic output in 2026 and 5% in 2027.

The IMF underscored the mantra it delivered during last week's annual meetings, urging policymakers to prioritize maintaining price stability, while preserving fiscal sustainability, maintaining central bank independence and enacting structural reforms to boost productivity and create jobs.
b237840acf467f0b: IPOH, Oct 22 — A study by Institut Darul Ridzuan (IDR), conducted in conjunction with the Perak 2027 Budget, has found that employment opportunities have overtaken the cost of living as the main concern among Perakians.

IDR chief executive Dr Zulqarnain Mohamad said the shift reflected changing public perceptions of current needs, particularly efforts to improve living standards and socioeconomic well-being in the state.

“The shift also highlights the importance of creating more jobs to ensure people have a stable source of income and can improve their living standards,” he told a press conference after the IDR dinner with Perak media practitioners here last night.
He said various state government initiatives, including the Pasar Sejahtera Rakyat programme, had helped address the cost of living and positively impacted people at the grassroots level.
Zulqarnain said the study also found that 66.4 per cent of respondents considered their monthly income sufficient, while 58.7 per cent said they could set aside emergency savings.
The findings indicated a positive overall picture of household finances, although individual households had different financial capacities depending on their commitments and expenditure.

Zulqarnain said the study also assessed psychological capital to gauge public confidence in the future and the state government’s ability to improve living standards, with the latter scoring 3.96 out of five, reflecting positive views on Perak’s socioeconomic prospects.

“That confidence must be backed by sustained efforts from all parties, including the state government, to expand job opportunities, increase incomes and improve the well-being of the people of Perak,” he said. — Bernama
19085f08e13c0231: PETALING JAYA: An oil palm plantation labourer was sentenced to nine months' imprisonment by the Batu Pahat magistrates' court in Johor today after pleading guilty to threatening his wife and chasing her with a parang over suspicions of infidelity.
Berita Harian reported that magistrate Mustaqim Sukarno sentenced Ahmad Fairus Mohamed, 42, after he pleaded guilty.
The court ordered that Fairus’s prison sentence run from the date of his arrest on Oct 18.
The father of three was charged with threatening his 37-year-old wife with a parang at a house in Senggarang at 8.30am on Oct 18.
The charge was framed under Section 506 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation, which provides for up to seven years' imprisonment if the threat is to cause death or grievous hurt.
According to the facts of the case, the incident occurred after an argument between Fairus and his wife. Fairus scolded and threatened her before grabbing a parang from a room and chasing her.
The woman ran to a neighbour’s house for help and lodged a report at the Senggarang police station that same day. Police arrested Fairus at 1.30pm.
The prosecution was led by deputy public prosecutor Nur Shahzleen Ibrahim while Fairus was represented by lawyer Kamarulariffin Nordin from the National Legal Aid Foundation.
b3648a4e65e0d731: ST PETERSBURG: Russia freed Stephen Hubbard, a retired US schoolteacher in custody since 2022, from prison on Wednesday and took him to St Petersburg to fly back to the US, after talks that Washington said were a step toward ending the war in Ukraine.

Russian President Vladimir Putin made the announcement at a meeting in St Petersburg with US envoy Steve Witkoff, who later said the talks will continue toward planned technical-level discussions involving the US, Russia and Ukraine.
Witkoff called Putin a "humanitarian" in thanking him for the move, a remark that drew sharp rebuke from Republican and Democratic lawmakers given Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

The prisoner release comes as president Donald Trump's recent gestures toward Moscow, including a deal to buy Russian diesel and a waiver of new sanctions, have already sparked bipartisan pushback in the US Congress and worry in European capitals.
Putin's spokesman, Dmitry Peskov, said Putin had freed Hubbard, 74, at Trump's request, and that he had also taken into account the American's poor health.
Trump later confirmed he had asked Putin on a call in recent days, and Putin agreed.

"The president sends his thanks, our whole nation sends their thanks, because of Stephen Hubbard," Witkoff told Putin in the meeting shown on Russian state TV. "Because of you he's going home to his family".
In a video shared with Reuters, Hubbard, wearing a dark fleece and clean-shaven, is seen in an undisclosed location in Russia shaking Witkoff's hand and thanking him.
Later, Trump posted a picture of Hubbard appearing inside a plane with others and holding an American flag.
Trump told reporters late on Wednesday that Hubbard had landed and that he would be visiting the White House "over the next day or so".
Hubbard's son, Joseph Coleman, told Reuters earlier in a voice message that he spoke briefly by phone with his father before he boarded the airplane in Russia.
"Today he seemed light in his step, a sense of happiness in his voice", Coleman said.
Three-way meeting planned on war
Witkoff called the talks with Putin "constructive" and said in a post on X that he had also met Ukrainian and European leaders in Oslo to advance Trump's mission to end the war.

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he supported the US proposal for three-way talks with Russia and the US at the level of negotiators to be held as soon as possible, preferably by early November.
Norwegian prime minister Jonas Gahr Stoere, who also met Witkoff, had earlier said the talks will likely happen in mid-November and focus on a potential post-conflict security structure.
On Wednesday evening, officials in Kyiv said Russian forces attacked the capital city with ballistic missiles that damaged homes and a petrol station and caused injuries.
'Humanitarian'
Witkoff's praise for Putin over Hubbard's release was scorned by some in Washington.
"Look up the definition of 'humanitarian.' What an embarrassing and outrageous thing to say," Republican US senator Thom Tillis said in an X post directed at the US envoy.

Trump, asked about Witkoff's "humanitarian" comment earlier on Wednesday, told reporters at the White House: “Well, I guess you have to say for that particular purpose, for the purpose of allowing a man, who was thinking he was going to be in prison for life, out. But I wouldn't say anything one way or the other".
"The US 'gave nothing in exchange' for the prisoner release," Trump said, adding "we're getting closer" to settling the war.

"He is the happiest man around," Trump said of Hubbard. "This was very surprising to him, but I did it, it really took place on a phone call at the end of last week with president Putin, so we appreciate it very much. And his family is extremely happy".
Family, lawyer disputed conviction
Hubbard, a native of Michigan, had been serving a prison sentence of six years and 10 months in Russia following a conviction for mercenary activity in a closed-door trial.
He was arrested in April 2022 in the eastern Ukrainian city of Izyum, where Russian prosecutors alleged he had been manning a Ukrainian military checkpoint.
Prosecutors said Hubbard had joined a Ukrainian territorial defence unit, received training, weapons and ammunition, and was promised $1,000 a month.

Russian state media reported he pleaded guilty to the charges. But Hubbard's US-based lawyer, Martin De Luca, previously told Reuters that Hubbard had told him the charges against him were false and that he was not in any combat or military unit.

In a 2024 interview with Reuters, Hubbard's sister, Patricia Hubbard Fox, also disputed the idea that her brother took up arms for any government, calling him "so non-military" and pointing out his advanced age.
De Luca on Wednesday thanked Trump, Witkoff and other US officials for securing the release, calling it "a dividend earned along the hard road to peace".
As of Wednesday, Hubbard was the only US prisoner held by Russia who was designated by Washington as "wrongfully detained".
The Trump administration secured the release last year of another American jailed in Russia, schoolteacher Marc Fogel, who had been serving a 14-year prison term for drug smuggling.
437cee29a012e6bd: SINGAPORE, Oct 22 — Expecting a new pair of AirPods, a Shopee customer was instead greeted by rows of staples when she opened the box delivered to her doorstep.

In a TikTok post on Tuesday (October 20), user momo043522 shared how she had purchased a pair of AirPods from Shopee Mall’s Apple Flagship Store, which claims to be an authorised Apple reseller with over 186,000 followers.
However, she was horrified to find stapler bullets in place of earphones inside the box she received.
“Where is my AirPods?” wrote momo043522 in her post, addressing Shopee.

The customer, identified only as Hu, told Stomp that she had ordered the AirPods on October 17 at 8.23pm for S$254 (RM812) on Shopee, after applying vouchers and the platform’s reward points system, Shopee Coins.
Checks on Shopee showed that the original price of the AirPods Pro 3 would cost S$349, although it is currently offering a 9 per cent platform discount.
It also claims the product is 100 per cent authentic and has a 4.9-star product rating based on over 9,000 reviews on Shopee.
Checks on Apple’s official online store show that the same pair of earbuds costs S$349.
Hu told Stomp that she received the parcel at her doorstep on October 18 and opened it around 2.30pm that day.
“The outer packaging was intact and I did not notice anything unusual,” said the 24-year-old teacher, adding that the seals on the box appeared to be untouched as well.
But when she found rows of staples inside the box, Hu said: “I was shocked and couldn’t believe my eyes.”
She shared that she had never experienced anything like this before and took the matter extremely seriously.
Refunded, but still ‘ridiculous’
Hu wrote that she immediately contacted Shopee’s customer service upon discovering the issue.
The seller reportedly requested for the AirPods’ serial number for investigation and instructed her to submit a return and refund request.
“We apologise for the inconvenience but please know that this is not what we want you to experience,” wrote the seller in a message to Hu.
It added that it was unaware of the matter as “all products are brand new and sealed”.
Hu shared that she had returned the item on October 19 and received a refund later that night.

“Later that night, I discovered that the seller had already issued my refund even before receiving the returned item,” Hu said, adding in the comments section of her post on October 20 that she was “surprised” by the quick refund but she still found the entire ordeal “absolutely ridiculous”.
She is hoping the seller will provide an explanation for the incident and also advised online shoppers to always record an unboxing video for expensive purchases.
“I also hope Shopee will strengthen its platform oversight, improve customer service and take cases like this seriously,” wrote Hu.
Shopee has taken ‘appropriate action’
A Shopee spokesperson told Stomp that it has looked into the matter and issued a full refund on October 19.
Shopee added that it has completed its investigation and taken appropriate action, including reviewing measures to prevent similar incidents.
The spokesperson also expressed thanks to the customer for raising the matter to the company.
The platform said: “Providing our customers with a safe and reliable shopping experience remains a key priority for Shopee.”
Hu’s post has amassed over 120,000 views on TikTok, with more than 3,300 likes and almost 4,000 shares.
AsiaOne has reached out to momo043522 for more information. — AsiaOne
901a55035f21ed4d: PETALING JAYA: Two former senior officers at Tabung Haji (TH) were charged today with cheating the agency’s board of directors in connection with the payment of RM3.3 billion in hibah (dividend distributions) for the 2017 financial year.

Former TH CEO Johan Abdullah, 70, and former TH chief financial officer Rozaida Omar, 63, pleaded not guilty after the joint charge was read out to them before judge Norma Ismail at the Kuala Lumpur sessions court.
According to the charge sheet, they allegedly deceived TH's board members by inducing them to approve inflated valuations of the organisation’s investment properties.

The charge sheet stated that both accused prepared and presented papers containing inflated property valuations in TH's unconsolidated financial statements for the financial year ended Dec 31, 2017, despite knowing that the properties should have been valued at lower market prices.
The alleged offence enabled TH to pay RM3.3 billion in hibah to depositors for the 2017 financial year.
The three properties involved were the TH Platinum Park building, TH Perdana building and TH Selborne building.
The offence was allegedly committed between 3pm and 10.30pm on Feb 9, 2018 at Menara TH Tun Razak along Jalan Tun Razak.
They were charged under Section 417 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same code. The offence carries a maximum jail term of five years, a fine or both, upon conviction.
The court set bail at RM60,000 with one surety for each accused and fixed Dec 8 for mention, pending the submission of documents.
Deputy public prosecutors Nazran Sham, Rohaiza Rahman and Siti Aina Rodhiah Shikh conducted the prosecution.
Rozaida was represented by lawyer Shamsul Sulaiman while Johan was represented by lawyers Shukri Mohamed and Malissa Shukri.
a6d0e3bbe3e539dd: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The split between PAS and Bersatu following an internal crisis in Perikatan Nasional (PN), which led to the cancellation of the coalition’s registration, could weaken the opposition’s position in the Melaka state election campaign beginning on Oct 31, political analysts say.

Ilham Centre research fellow Mujibu Abd Muis said the opposition’s internal turmoil would affect coordination of election strategies, potentially leading to multi-cornered contests, a split in votes and candidates from opposition parties competing against one another.
He said PN’s deregistration raised questions about using a common identity and coordinating candidates, prompting PAS and Bersatu to reconsider their strategies for the state election.

“PAS may find it easier to campaign under its own identity because it has a strong organisational network and grassroots support. Nevertheless, this does not guarantee that it will retain all the support voters previously gave to PN.
“Without coordination, multi-cornered contests could lead to vote splitting, giving rival parties an advantage.
“The Melaka state election will test not only the strength of PAS and Bersatu, but also their ability to adjust their strategies in the wake of the split,” he told Bernama.

Mujibu, a senior political science lecturer at Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM), said Bersatu faced a bigger immediate challenge in charting its political direction without relying on its strategic alliance with PAS.
He said Bersatu could either operate independently to preserve its political identity or seek new alliances, although both options posed risks to its long-term future.
“Bersatu may be able to maintain its political autonomy by flying solo, but autonomy without strategic partners could become an electoral liability,” he said.

He said the rift between PAS and Bersatu could also reshape the opposition’s political landscape, particularly in determining which party could inherit the influence and support previously consolidated under PN.

He said PAS was well placed to become a more dominant force within the opposition bloc, given its organisational capacity and grassroots reach, but it would need to prove itself by winning seats and attracting support beyond its existing base.

Meanwhile, Universiti Malaya socio-political analyst Datuk Professor Dr Awang Azman Awang Pawi said the crisis in PN could hasten a realignment among opposition parties, including changes to relations between PAS, Bersatu and other parties.
He said the possibility of an alternative coalition or a more flexible political alliance could not be discounted if the former BN component parties failed to restore their working relationship.

He said the approaching Oct 31 nomination day for the Melaka state election left PAS and Bersatu with little time to resolve uncertainties over party symbols, seat allocation and campaign coordination.

“The crisis could lead to former allies competing against one another, overlapping candidates and confusion among supporters if legal issues and political disagreements are not resolved quickly,” he said.

Nevertheless, he said PN’s deregistration would not automatically weaken the opposition, as PAS and Bersatu retained their respective organisational structures, grassroots networks and political influence.

The Registrar of Societies Malaysia (RoS) cancelled PN’s registration on Tuesday (Oct 20) under subparagraph 13(1)(c)(iv) of the Societies Act 1966 after finding that the coalition’s explanation had failed to refute the grounds for cancellation set out in a notice dated Sept 22.

The decision came after an internal crisis within PN, when Bersatu submitted a formal complaint to RoS on Aug 11, alleging it had been barred from attending and participating in a PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16. — Bernama
3b24d666a3eb7111: PETALING JAYA: Dua bekas pegawai kanan Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) mengaku tidak bersalah di Mahkamah Sesyen Kuala Lumpur atas tuduhan memperdaya ahli lembaga pengarah berkait pembayaran hibah berjumlah RM3.3 bilion bagi tahun kewangan 2017.
Bekas ketua pegawai kewangan TH, Rozaida Omar dan bekas ketua pegawai eksekutif, Johan Abdullah membuat pengakuan itu selepas pertuduhan dibacakan di hadapan Hakim Norma Ismail, lapor Berita Harian.

Mengikut pertuduhan, Rozaida, 63, dan Johan, 70, didakwa secara bersama memperdaya ahli lembaga pengarah TH dengan mendorong mereka meluluskan penilaian semula hartanah pelaburan organisasi berkenaan yang dilambungkan nilainya.

Mereka didakwa menyediakan dan membentangkan kertas kerja mengandungi penilaian hartanah yang dilambungkan dalam penyata kewangan belum dikonsolidasi bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 31 Dis 2017, sedangkan mengetahui hartanah itu sepatutnya dinilai pada harga pasaran yang lebih rendah.
Hartanah itu ialah Bangunan TH Platinum Park, Bangunan TH Perdana dan Bangunan TH Selborne.
Menurut pertuduhan, perbuatan itu bagi membolehkan TH membuat pembayaran hibah berjumlah RM3.3 bilion kepada pendeposit bagi tahun kewangan 2017.
Mereka didakwa melakukan kesalahan itu antara 3 petang hingga 10.30 malam di Menara TH Tun Razak, Jalan Tun Razak, pada 9 Feb 2018.

Rozaida dan Johan didakwa mengikut Seksyen 417 Kanun Keseksaan dibaca bersama Seksyen 34 kanun sama, yang memperuntukkan hukuman penjara maksimum lima tahun atau denda atau kedua-duanya sekali, jika sabit kesalahan.

Hakim kemudiannya membenarkan kedua-dua tertuduh masing-masing dibebaskan dengan ikat jamin RM60,000 dengan seorang penjamin dan menetapkan 8 Dis sebagai tarikh sebutan semula kes bagi penyerahan dokumen.

Pendakwaan dikendalikan Timbalan Pendakwah Raya, Nazran Mohd Sham, Rohaiza Abd Rahman dan Siti Aina Rodhiah Md Shikh menakala Rozaida diwakili peguam Shamsul Sulaiman dan Johan diwakili Shukri Mohamed serta Malissa Shukri.
f078c490613d8717: SINGAPORE, Oct 22 — An Immigration and Checkpoints Authority (ICA) officer was under the influence of alcohol when he drove and crashed his car into a concrete barrier on the side of a slip road into Loyang Avenue.
But Ken Ong Wei Qi later lied to the police about only consuming alcoholic drinks after driving.

The 35-year-old, who held the rank of Assistant Superintendent of Police at the time of the incident on June 14, 2025, admitted in court on October 19 to offences including drink driving and providing false information to a public servant.
On Thursday (October 22), he was sentenced to three weeks’ jail, fined S$6,500 (RM20,780) and disqualified from holding or obtaining all classes of driving licences for 36 months.
An ICA spokesperson said in response to AsiaOne’s queries that Ong was immediately reassigned to administrative duties after the accident.
He subsequently resigned from ICA on October 19, the day of his conviction.
Breath alcohol content double the legal limit
According to court documents, the accident occurred along the Tampines Expressway in the direction of Seletar Expressway, at the slip road into Loyang Avenue, sometime after 2am.
Ong had decided to drive to Pasir Ris from Prinsep Street, after failing to find a designated driver, reported Shin Min Daily News.
The abandoned vehicle was discovered by patrolling police officers at about 3.50am. They noted that the car was damaged, with no one inside.
At about 4.30am, the ex-ICA officer returned to the scene.
He failed a breathalyser test, but claimed he had only consumed alcohol at home. He also said he did not collide with anything.
His breath alcohol content was 76 microgrammes of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath, more than double the legal limit of 35 microgrammes.
Ong repeated his lie at the traffic police headquarters later that same morning, claiming he had two or three cans of beer at home after driving the car and before returning to the scene.
On June 19, 2026, he finally admitted to having driven drunk.
The ICA spokesperson said the agency takes a serious view of misconduct by its officers.

“ICA officers are expected to maintain a high standard of integrity and professionalism at all times,” it added. “ICA officers who break the law will be dealt with, in accordance with the law.” — AsiaOne
06101e9ea8baed65: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 22 — A man and his female companion were killed after their motorcycle was struck by a vehicle in a hit-and-run crash along the Tun Dr Lim Chong Eu Expressway near the Penang Bridge interchange early this morning.

Timur Laut District Police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said initial investigations found that the crash occurred at about 4 am as the 22-year-old man and 20-year-old woman were travelling from George Town towards Penang Bridge.
“Upon reaching the junction leading to Penang Bridge and Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM), their motorcycle was believed to have been hit from behind by an unidentified vehicle.
“Both victims, from Padang Serai, Kedah, died at the scene,” he said in a statement today.
Abdul Rozak said their bodies were taken to the Forensic Medicine Department at Penang Hospital for post-mortem.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
Police urged anyone with information about the crash to contact investigating officer Insp Shahidatul Alyaa Nordin at 019-6886106. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: ACP stands for Assistant Commissioner of Police.
a682785a476e5430: SEPANG, Oct 22 — As the government encourages Malaysians to consider switching from Waze to locally developed navigation applications, TuJu offers motorists an alternative that combines navigation with live traffic information and highway-related services.
Developed by the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) in collaboration with Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd (PCSB), TuJu was officially launched on November 26, 2025.
Unlike conventional navigation applications that focus primarily on directions and traffic conditions, TuJu also incorporates services specific to Malaysian highways.
Here is what motorists should know about the application.
Who developed TuJu?
TuJu was developed through a collaboration between LLM and PCSB.
LLM oversees Malaysia’s highway network, providing the institutional context for an application designed to bring navigation and highway-related information together for motorists.
What can TuJu do?
TuJu provides navigation with directions, journey distances and estimated arrival times to help motorists plan their routes.
Its live traffic information allows users to monitor road conditions, while CCTV feeds at selected highway locations let them check traffic visually before or during their journeys.
Motorists can also check toll fares and look up facilities at rest and recreation (R&R) areas along highways to plan stops during longer journeys.
The application also links to the Works Ministry’s MyJalan platform, which allows users to report road damage and other infrastructure problems.
How does TuJu differ from other navigation apps?
TuJu brings navigation together with services linked to highway management and government infrastructure.
Its SOS button provides another avenue for users to seek emergency assistance, complementing the highway-related contact information available through the application.
These functions, alongside its integration with MyJalan, distinguish TuJu as a navigation option that incorporates highway-related services beyond route guidance.
LLM to be a traffic information provider
According to LLM deputy director-general (operations) Mohammed Ridzuan Jahidin, TuJu focuses on providing traffic info, not collecting user data.
The focus, he said, is on supplying motorists with live traffic information instead of depending on data contributed by users.
The approach is relevant amid concerns over personal data collection and the government’s encouragement for Malaysians to consider locally developed alternatives to Waze.
What new features are available on TuJu 2.0?
According to details provided during an earlier briefing, TuJu 2.0 introduces additional features, including information on electric vehicle-related facilities, roadblocks and saved destinations.
Users can save frequently visited locations and identify where they have parked their vehicles, including in large parking areas.
TuJu 2.0 is currently available on Android, while the iOS version was still undergoing testing and will likely be available on App Store by year-end.
What else is LLM planning for TuJu?
Mohammed Ridzuan said LLM hoped to incorporate a payment system into the application to make it easier for motorists to pay toll fares.
The proposed addition would expand TuJu’s existing services, although further details on its implementation were not provided.
624c3fad09d3845c: SINGAPORE, Oct 22 — Residents in Singapore on Thursday (October22) woke up to better air quality for a fifth consecutive day — a run that began on October2218.

While hourly PM2.5 and 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) have not returned to levels recorded before September 4, when air quality entered the unhealthy range for the first time this year, hourly concentration readings have stayed in the normal to low-elevated bands over the past days.
The improvement came as winds turned to blow from the south.
At 8am, PM2.5 was in the normal band across Singapore.
Meanwhile, PSI was in the good-to-moderate range in all regions, except in western Singapore with a low-unhealthy PSI of 108.
In its daily haze situation update on Wednesday evening, the National Environment Agency (NEA) cautioned that smoke haze may still be transported towards Singapore on Thursday and Friday.
It pointed out that while showers are forecast over Singapore and the surrounding region, dry conditions are again expected over the southern parts of Kalimantan.

This, coupled with the prevailing east-southeasterly or south-easterly winds, means that smoke haze from fires in Kalimantan may be transported towards Singapore — with the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) forecast to be between 101 and 160 — in the unhealthy range.
The situation is forecast to persist into Friday.
Members of the public should check the latest concentration readings before participating in any outdoor activities.
Employers should take note of the Ministry of Manpower's Tuesday additional guidance to adjust outdoor work based on the hourly PM2.5 readings. — AsiaOne
394ae4e44f991d20: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The government is enhancing the locally developed navigation app, TuJu, by expanding its coverage beyond highways to ordinary roads to improve traffic information and user experience, the Dewan Rakyat was told today.
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the move followed public feedback calling for more comprehensive navigation services.

He said TuJu, created by the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) under the Works Ministry in collaboration with Prosignal Consortium Sdn Bhd (PCSB), was originally designed to monitor highway traffic and provide access to closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage.
“I agree with those who say the service needs further improvement, and we are looking into it.
“The app is being expanded to cover not only highways but also traffic conditions on ordinary roads.

“GovTech will work closely with relevant agencies to develop and enhance the capabilities of this local app,” he said in response to Young Syefura Othman (PH-Bentong) on the readiness and performance of local navigation apps compared with foreign alternatives.
Meanwhile, Gobind said the Waze ban applied only to civil servants conducting official government business, citing data security and legal risks.
The ban does not apply to general members of the public using the app for personal purposes, he said.
However, he stressed that civil servants were not restricted to using the TuJu app, and could continue using alternatives, including Google Maps, for official duties.
According to Gobind, Waze’s terms of service fall under Israeli legal jurisdiction, raising concerns over movement data security and potential difficulties in seeking legal recourse.
Responding to Young Syefura’s original question on GovTech’s progress, the minister said 62 services from 22 government agencies had been integrated into the MyGov Malaysia app as of Oct 8.

The app has recorded more than 3.19 million downloads and over 3.01 million active users, enabling Malaysians to access services such as paying traffic fines, replacing MyKad identity cards and checking unclaimed money online. — Bernama
b1a06af4221b6500: BEIJING: The Chinese AI pioneer DeepSeek has raised about ¥100 billion (US$15 billion) in its latest fundraising round, one of the country’s largest ever and a sign of the startup’s ambitions to compete globally with the likes of Anthropic PBC and OpenAI.

The Hangzhou-based firm boosted its financing target at least twice as it talked with investors, from ¥50 billion to ¥80 billion before reaching the final tally, according to people familiar with the matter.

Battery pioneer Contemporary Amperex Technology Co Ltd (CATL) and WeChat-operator Tencent Holdings Ltd were among the biggest investors in the round, said the people, asking not to be named as the details aren’t public.
DeepSeek’s funding sets the stage for one of the most highly anticipated Chinese market debuts in years.

The AI upstart triggered a US$1 trillion meltdown in global markets in 2025 when it showed the ability to compete with Silicon Valley’s leaders at a fraction of the cost of their models, but it’s never had the financial resources of the US frontier labs.
The latest fundraising shows that imbalance is beginning to moderate, although it still has far less financial firepower than Anthropic and OpenAI, which have each raised more than US$100 billion.
Like rival Moonshot, DeepSeek is preparing for an initial public offering that would be an important milestone for Chinese markets, Bloomberg News has reported.
DeepSeek has begun to spend more aggressively to build out AI data centres and to develop more open-source models for use in China and abroad.
The firm has regularly rolled out high-performance, low-cost models that put pressure on its domestic competitors and gained customers in the US and other overseas markets.
In September, for example, it dropped V4.1 Flash, setting off a drop in the share prices of local rivals MiniMax Group Inc and Z.AI Co.
DeepSeek, Tencent and CATL representatives didn’t respond to emailed requests for comment.
More broadly, companies from Alibaba Group Holding Ltd to ByteDance Ltd have introduced low-cost AI services, typically open-sourced so customers can modify them as needed.

One widely shared benchmark chart from Artificial Analysis sketched out what has been called the “DeepSeek death zone,” where competitors will struggle to survive if they can’t beat the firm’s performance or they can’t charge lower prices.
20274e99f20c805a: SAN FRANCISCO, Oct 22 — A New Mexico judge ruled Wednesday that Meta must pay US$25 billion (RM102 billion) to the state after a jury found last month that the social media giant had deceived users in a case related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal, according to media reports.
The penalty comes a couple of months after Meta agreed to pay US$18 billion to settle claims brought by 48 other states, including allegations tied to Cambridge Analytica.
Meta slammed the case as “a tax on speech.”
“This ruling... makes it all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico,” Meta said in a statement. “We are confident we will prevail on appeal.”

Cambridge Analytica was a political consulting firm found to have improperly harvested personal data from millions of Facebook users for targeted political advertising, notably during the 2016 US presidential election.

Revelations at the time showed that the firm had obtained data gathered through a personality quiz app called “thisisyourdigitallife,” which was installed by about 270,000 users but also collected information on their friends.
In total, the app reached roughly 87 million Facebook users worldwide.
Facebook learned in December 2015 that Cambridge Analytica had acquired the data but did not disclose it publicly until 2018, after a whistleblower came forward, sparking a major political scandal.
Jurors in the New Mexico trial found that the misconduct affected all of the state’s more than 2.1 million residents.
“We disagree with the verdict and will continue to defend ourselves against efforts to distort our record,” a Meta spokesperson said in a statement in September.
New Mexico Attorney General Raul Torrez hailed the ruling as a “historic” win.

This case was “about whether corporations can mislead consumers about what happens to their personal information without facing meaningful consequences. New Mexico stood its ground,” Torrez said in a statement.
Penalties pile up
Meta has faced a slew of lawsuits in recent months.
Earlier this year, New Mexico won nearly US$1 billion in combined penalties against Meta in a separate case over harms to children.
In March, a jury in that case ordered Meta to pay US$375 million after finding the company liable for endangering children by making them vulnerable to predators on its platforms, among other harms.
In August, a judge ordered Meta to implement product changes and pay an additional US$567 million to the state to fund the treatment and prevention of harms caused by Facebook and Instagram.

That same month, Meta agreed to pay up to US$17.7 billion to 52 US states, plus Washington, DC, to settle claims that it deliberately engineered its platforms to hook young users, misled the public about the risks and unlawfully collected data from children under 13.

As part of that settlement, Meta agreed to make significant changes to Facebook and Instagram accounts used by teenagers, and portions of the settlement hinge on other major social media companies agreeing to similar changes.
In September, TikTok agreed to pay Alabama at least US$100 million and enact limits for teen users, avoiding a trial over claims related to child safety on the platform.
TikTok previously settled other cases that were headed for trial, including a Los Angeles lawsuit brought by a young woman and a suit from a Kentucky school district.
In a landmark trial that concluded in March, Meta and YouTube were convicted by a Los Angeles jury, which found both companies were responsible for a teenager’s social media addiction.
That jury awarded the teenager US$6 million. — AFP
a04f86dcd04cd451: WASHINGTON, Oct 22 — US President Donald Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff faced criticism Wednesday for calling Vladimir Putin a “humanitarian” despite the Russian leader’s brutal war in Ukraine.
Witkoff made the comments as he met Putin in Saint Petersburg to secure the release of Stephen Hubbard, an American citizen who was detained for years after being arrested in Ukraine.
“You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian — you are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that,” Witkoff said, referring to Hubbard’s release.
“I commend you, and I thank you again.”
The Kremlin said after the meeting between Witkoff and Putin that Russia was ready in principle to rejoin three-way talks with Ukraine and the United States to end the war.
But Witkoff’s comments come as Trump’s recent pivot away from Ukraine and towards Putin — the man who launched the biggest war in Europe since World War II — faces growing increasing scrutiny.
Republican Senator Thom Tillis, a frequent Trump critic in recent months, reacted with astonishment.
“WTF, Steve? Look up the definition of ‘humanitarian’,” he said in a post on X.
Trump brushed off the comments by Witkoff — a business friend whom he appointed roving envoy for the Ukraine, Iran and Gaza conflicts after he took office last year.

“Well, I guess you could say (it) for that particular purpose, for the purpose of allowing a man who was thinking he was going to be in prison for life out,” Trump said when asked about his envoy’s remarks.
“But you know, I wouldn’t say anything one way or the other.”
US Vice President JD Vance defended Witkoff’s comments.
“I agree with Steve Witkoff saying something nice to a person who just released an American hostage,” Vance said at an event in Ohio.
“Whether you agree with the underlying sentiment or not, Steve Witkoff is a diplomat. His job is to go over there and get a job done.” — AFP

c509d28c742ec833: OCTOBER 22 — In the wake of high-profile school violence cases, the phrase “Syukurlah Malaysia masih aman (Thank goodness Malaysia is still peaceful)” feels a little shakier. Many are rightly shocked and concerned for our children. Having physical and online discussions and sharing information feels helpful, but where do we draw the line between solidarity and sensationalism?

Amidst the most recent case in Kuching, I strongly urge the public to stop spreading photos or videos of school violence incidents and the media to practise ethical, non-sensationalist reporting to prevent the social contagion effect, which may lead to copycat incidents.
In the age of virality and artificial intelligence, Malaysians must do the same: stop sharing school violence photos and videos. — Picture by Yusof Isa

Social contagion is a psychological phenomenon where behaviours, emotions, or ideas spread quickly and spontaneously through groups, often without individuals being aware of the influence. The social contagion theory helps explain how group dynamics and social trends are shaped.

In the United States (USA), there have been numerous studies on whether mass media coverage influences mass shootings. A 2015 study found that mass killings involving firearms (including school shootings) were motivated by similar events in the immediate past. On average, this temporary increase in probability lasts 13 days. Outside this period, perpetrators of particularly horrific massacres like Virginia Tech, Sandy Hook, and Umpqua Community College clearly cited mass killers before them as inspiration for their attacks.

As ethical, non-sensationalised reporting was adopted in the USA to stem a wave of teen suicides in the 1980s, experts have called for a similar approach to gun violence. Besides stricter gun laws, campaigns like the “Don’t Name Them” movement have urged the media and the public to stop profiling or sensationalising the shooters and focus on victims and survivors so that the shooters do not get the fame they seek.

Although guns are difficult to obtain in Malaysia, anything can be a weapon if misused with intent and sufficient force. Metal detectors, police presence, CCTVs, and the rotan will only provide a false sense of safety if we fail to address the core reasons for school violence.

After the Kuching case, I was very disheartened to find social media posts with hashtags like #viralkan and #fyp. These hashtags boost the post’s algorithm, making them appear on people’s feeds. They exploit legitimate shock and concerns on school safety, which generate the “Likes” and “Shares” and sometimes, income for the poster.

Even when it is well meant, we can discuss school violence without publicising the perpetrator’s livestream of the attack or manifesto. The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) can only do so much. Despite their user policies, social media platforms do not have strong incentive to remove content because their business models thrive on outrage and virality.

We say that children are susceptible to the influence of social media; social contagion explains that adults are not immune. So, we must confront ourselves: are we sharing because we really care or because our brains thrive on the endorphin rush from online validation?

In the age of virality and artificial intelligence (AI), Malaysians must do the same: stop sharing school violence photos and videos. Let’s get off our devices, let’s get down to business, and deal with the hard issues to stop school violence.
* This is the personal opinion of the writer or publication and does not necessarily represent the views of Malay Mail.

5d4301edaabed16d: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — As Malaysia rapidly ages, it needs a targeted approach, with a ministry dedicated to older persons and one agency to coordinate all aged care policies.

Ezzati Nasir, CEO and founder of Teman Malaysia, which provides care companion services for older persons, said the country’s approach to aged care is currently fragmented across different ministries.
“I do hope that when I am an aged person, there will be a Ministry for Older Persons,” she said as a panellist at the National Long-Term Care Financing Dialogue yesterday.

Instead of “wasting time” by having different ministries decide which areas of aged care or matters relating to older persons fall within their scope or responsibilities, she said it is better to have a dedicated ministry.
“So I feel we have to come together and work on elderly care as one holistic approach and one ministry,” she said.

Malaysia Productivity Corporation Private Healthcare Productivity Nexus champion Datuk Dr Jacob Thomas said the Malaysian government should set up an agency to set policy and coordinate efforts on care for older persons.

“What I’m hoping for and I think we are getting there is for one agency – a Cabinet-directed body – to manage aged care, just like what you have in Japan, in Australia,” he said in a separate panel at the same dialogue.

He added that this agency would not leave out any ministries: “The Ministry of Health will have to play a critical role. The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development will have to play a role and I hear that they are going to take the lead in this, supported by the Ministry of Health and the others. Ministry of Finance has to come in.
“So, all of them have to come in, but there has to be someone to drive it.”
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Malaysia Productivity Corporation’s Datuk Dr Jacob Thomas said the Cabinet needs to appoint or direct an agency to coordinate different ministries on all matters related to aged care. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin

Dr Jacob based his proposal on Malaysia’s experience with medical tourism, which was handled by different departments until the government set up the Malaysia Healthcare Travel Council under the Ministry of Health.
“After that things took off in a big way because everybody was listening to that one agency who was coordinating the activities around the whole continuum of medical tourism.
“So, similarly for aged care, there are many players. Social welfare, there’s finance, there’s a Ministry of Health, all of them have to be coordinated,” he said.

In another panel discussion, Malaysian Caregivers Association (Kendana) chairman Rashidi Yahaya also said Malaysia needs an “anchor ministry” to take charge of long-term care, and that a ministry has to step forward to play this role.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Datuk Tengku Aizan Tengku Abdul Hamid (second left) said coordinating government efforts on ageing through a single agency could avoid duplicating efforts and wasting limited resources. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin

Datuk Tengku Aizan Tengku Abdul Hamid, Academy of Sciences Malaysia council member and Private Pension Administrator Malaysia board chairman, also said Malaysia urgently needs to create an agency for ageing, instead of continuing with a fragmented approach to such policies.
“The most critical one from my observation is for us to look at the coordination across sectors of and levels of government. I think that is very critical because we have been doing silo work.
“We have limited resources, so we don’t want to be redundant and wasteful, but we want to achieve the same output. So the end goal is the same,” she said.
She added that there is a need for different agencies to work together and reduce the mentality of “pacak bendera” or staking claim over different initiatives.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

Temasek Polytechnic gerontology lecturer Nurdiyanah Kamsan (right) said it could be helpful for Malaysia to have an agency where caregivers could find information on the services and support available to them. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin

Nurdiyanah Kamsan, who lectures on gerontology at Singapore’s Temasek Polytechnic, said it would be helpful to have a one-stop integrated agency that could provide resources on caregiving and ageing services to first-time caregivers, such as those whose parents have just been diagnosed with dementia.

“Would it be helpful if you have one integrated agency that you can sort of, you know, put your foot in there and ‘Okay, these are the services that I need to go, or these are the community places that can help me’. So, a consolidated agency like that would be very helpful,” she said at another panel discussion.
“On top of that, this particular agency must work with the community on the ground to understand the services that are needed within communities,” she said.
The dialogue was organised by Kendana together with Universiti Putra Malaysia’s Malaysian Research Institute on Ageing.
In November 2025, the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development launched the Malaysia Care Strategic Framework and Action Plan (2026–2030).
That document stated that both the ministry and the Ministry of Health have been appointed co-leads for long-term care.
Long-term care refers to care and support, typically for older persons who cannot meet their basic needs independently.

Among other things, the action plan includes the planned coordination of the different standard operating procedures across ministries and regulatory agencies for the registration and licensing of care centres.
Also included in the action plan is the planned setting up of a National Care Regulatory Body to oversee the registration, licensing, accreditation and quality assurance of care providers.

The Health Ministry’s 2023 Health White Paper also recognised the need to strengthen inter-agency and inter-sectoral collaboration to improve health outcomes for Malaysians, and proposed formalising an inter-ministerial taskforce on healthy ageing and aged care.

672962236d553051: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The High Court today rejected a bid by the teenager acquitted of murdering his schoolmate Yap Shing Xuen at a Bandar Utama secondary school last year to have the entire civil suit heard in-camera, or in closed-door proceedings.

Judicial Commissioner Datuk Anand Ponnudurai said there was no basis for the broader order sought by the teenager, through his counsel, to hold the entire proceedings in-camera, excluding members of the media and anyone not directly involved in the case.

Anand said the court could not determine at this stage which witnesses would testify or the nature of their evidence, adding that the defendants could later apply for specific witnesses to testify in-camera if their evidence was likely to identify the teenager.
“The court is cognisant of the Child Act 2001, which restricts the reporting of details identifying a child, and also of the interest of justice and the public interest.
“There are many cases in which orders are granted to protect a child, but the proceedings are still conducted with the media allowed to report, subject to restrictions.
“Considering the nature of this case and the necessity to protect the child/first defendant (D1), I am of the view that a balancing act is required.

“While the child must be protected, I see no reason for a total ban on reporting. There will be benefits to the public in knowing what transpires and in the judgment,” he said in his ruling earlier today.

Nevertheless, Anand ordered a ban on publishing any information that could identify the teenager, and directed that all cause papers be sealed and kept confidential, accessible only to the parties and their solicitors.
He also ordered that the names of D1, his litigation representative and his parents be anonymised and referred to only by their initials.

Lawyer Surendra Ananth appeared for Yap’s family, while Nicholas Poon represented the teenager, Abraham Au appeared for the boy’s parents and senior federal counsel Liew Horng Bin represented the government agencies.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

In the current lawsuit filed on October 1, Yap’s family — her mother (pic) and sister — claimed that breaches of duty of care contributed to her death in October last year. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
Background
In the current lawsuit filed on October 1, Yap’s family — her mother and sister — claimed that breaches of duty of care contributed to her death in October last year.
Among those named are the boy himself, his parents, and several school authorities, including his homeroom teacher, the school principal, and teachers responsible for counselling and student affairs.

The family also named officers from the Petaling Utama district education office, the Selangor education department director, the director-general of education, the education minister, the registrar general of educational institutions and teachers, the director-general of health, the health minister, the women, family and community development minister and the government of Malaysia.

Yap’s mother, who is also suing as the estate administrator and in her own right, is seeking special damages totalling RM120,602 for her daughter’s funeral expenses from the named defendants jointly and separately.
She is also separately seeking general damages to be assessed by the High Court, including any other relief the court deems fit or appropriate.

On September 14, the Shah Alam High Court acquitted and discharged the teenager after finding he was of unsound mind at the time of the offence, and ordered him to be placed at Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta for a period subject to the Sultan of Selangor’s approval.
The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) has since filed an appeal challenging the acquittal.
626828ddb48132ba: PARIS, Oct 22 — Police banned protests in parts of Paris on Thursday, as France braced for more demonstrations just days after student and other rallies degenerated into some of the worst street unrest in years.

Wednesday’s announcement came after President Emmanuel Macron took an apparent swipe at his US counterpart Donald Trump for exploiting the riots for political advantage in the US midterm election battle.

The Paris ban will last from 8:00 am to 8:00 pm (0600 to 1800 GMT) and apply to key landmarks in the French capital, including the Elysee presidential palace, both houses of parliament, as well as tourist havens such as the Louvre museum and the Champs-Elysees.
Other areas where rallies will be prohibited include the Bastille and Republique squares, and the Chatelet-Les Halles shopping area which was heavily targeted by looters over the weekend.
France has admitted it “lost control” in the frenzy of street violence that erupted last weekend, when masked youths clashed with police, looted shops and vandalised public buildings.

As his government struggled to contain a crisis that has damaged France’s image abroad and rattled financial markets six months before presidential elections, Macron implied that Trump, and possibly Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is also fighting an election campaign, made “stupid comments” on the unrest for political gain.
“There are people who campaign at France’s expense — leaders who are in campaign mode, whether here in the region or on the other side of the Atlantic,” he told reporters in Doha.
Trump has sought to link the unrest to “migrants, jihadists, and communists” as he campaigned for his Republican party in the United States on his anti-immigration messaging.
He also on Tuesday hailed French far-right leader Marine Le Pen, who shares his ideologies.
Le Pen late Wednesday branded Macron’s remarks as “conspiratorial” in a post on X.

“The images we saw last Saturday are not generated by artificial intelligence: they show the sad reality of what France has become after 10 years of Macronist rule,” added the far-right candidate, who is leading in the polls for the 2027 presidential election.
Several analysts have dismissed the claims that migrants were driving France’s protests.
‘New phase’ upcoming

The unrest overshadowed demonstrations held Saturday in which more than half a million people marched nationwide against the cost of living. Those rallies followed four weeks of student protests that have closed many schools across France.
Since the rioting — the worst France has seen in years — and ahead of fresh cost-of-living demonstrations planned for Saturday, Macron’s government has warned it will brook no further violence.
Fresh demonstrations planned by high school pupils and university students were similarly struck down in both Paris and the southeastern city of Lyon.
Following a meeting on Wednesday with Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu, the leader of France’s hardline CGT union, Sophie Binet, called for a “new phase” of protests, with strikes early next month.
Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said Wednesday that, of the 2,500 people taken into custody during and after the protests, 174 had been jailed. Another 917 had been formally prosecuted, he added.
The convulsion in the EU’s second-biggest economy has rattled financial markets already nervous about the country’s growing debt pile and deficit.
The yield on France’s benchmark 10-year bond passed five per cent on Wednesday as investors demanded a higher return amid fiscal concerns.
On Friday, the Moody’s ratings agency is expected to lower its grade on France’s public debt.
‘Quite disconcerting’
France’s neighbours Italy and Belgium were also experiencing similar unrest, on a smaller scale. Italy’s government has ordered 500 troops to Milan to stem street violence there.
While the curfews imposed in several cities have helped calm the situation, they have disrupted some access to late-night public transport.

“It’s quite disconcerting,” said one Paris commuter who gave only his first name, Louis, when he found his line closed. But “if it can prevent further acts of vandalism... then yes, I think it’s a good thing”, he said.

The Yellow Vest movement behind last weekend’s demonstrations announced Wednesday it plans a march on Saturday from Bastille square in Paris, and follow-up nationwide demonstrations on November 5. — AFP

234ff1651b0c813f: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna has told investors that open weight models now make brilliant sense for on-prem enterprise use.
Speaking on the company’s Q3 earnings call, Krishna said that in 2024 closed frontier models were plainly superior to open alternatives.
“If you ran some assessment, some benchmark, and it was broad-based, not narrow, the top model might score a 70, and the open model might score a 20 or a 30.”
“In late 2025, we began to see that gap shrink, where maybe the gap was not 70 to 20 or 30, it was 70 to 50,” he continued.

The CEO said open weight models currently deliver “anywhere from 25 percent to 10 percent of the token cost of the frontier models. That is very attractive given that they’re now 90 percent as effective.”
“It’s a simple question for any enterprise. Would you like something that’s 10 percent of the cost if it’s 90 percent as good as the best, or do you want to pay that 10 times higher cost?”
Krishna thinks businesses will most often choose not to incur the higher costs.

“Then the question is: how many tasks require that? I would tell you some do, but the vast majority, summarizing an email, examining a contract, answering a customer call, composing an email, all of those can be done as well with the much cheaper answer.”

The CEO said those numbers mean IBM is seeing booming interest in on-prem AI infrastructure. While he thinks most businesses can build useful AI infrastructure in just two or three racks, he feels many will struggle to get it running.

“The question becomes: how do you do that?” he said. “The question that the enterprise struggles with is: ‘Where are my kernel engineers? Where are the people who worry about the underlying network? Who can make sure that the model is clustered on GPUs that are close to each other in network proximity? Who can make sure that you’re doing the right caching of results so you get an incredible response?’”

He didn’t have answers, other than to say IBM will produce software that eases AI deployments. Krishna also predicted demand for on-prem AI will spur sales of Big Blue’s Spyre mainframe accelerator cards.

The CEO said current-gen z17 mainframes have delivered $1bn more revenue than any previous model, and said Big Blue’s new rackable models delivered “the strongest midrange launch in IBM Z in nearly two decades.” Mainframe revenue, however, fell 20 percent – as IBM expects given it’s now 18 months since it launched the z17.
IBM’s infrastructure revenue grew five percent year-over-year to $3.7 billion, much slower improvement than recorded by rivals Dell, HPE, and Lenovo.

Software did rather better, scoring nine percent growth to reach $7.8 billion for the quarter. Red Hat was the star, growing eleven percent and increasing annual recurring revenue by 30 percent. Some of that future revenue is for Red Hat’s virtualization products, which have now won $800 million of deals, with a pipeline of a further $750 million. That’s a solid result for a product line launched in 2024, and IBM believes there’s more to come given the possibility some VMware users are on the move.
Total quarterly revenue hit $17.1 billion, up five percent. IBM’s share price wobbled in after-hours trading and ended down a point or two.

Another IBM matter The Register is watching today is a severity one incident in the Big Blue cloud, caused by “emergency maintenance” that meant users could not provision new resources or virtual private clouds for 90 minutes. Users of IBM’s Classic Cloud, the service it acquired from SoftLayer in 2013, have been told Big Blue will “restore new provisioning and resource management in our Classic environment” by 08:00 UTC on Thursday – meaning the incident will last at least 16 hours.

Bukan sahaja kata bodoh, sebetulnya Ummi mempertikaikan tindakan mempertahankan rasuah dan korupsi dengan menyebut-nyebut perihal skandal Tabung Haji dan lain-lain. Ini adalah intipati yang sepatutnya menjadi sorotan.

Meskipun berbahasa Inggeris, kata bodoh yang digunakan memang menular menjadi racun dalam pembuluh darah ramai penyokong Najib. Selepas keratan video itu menjadi tular, ramai dalam kalangan ahli Umno di media sosial ‘menghunus keris’ kepada siswi ini. Ada yang malah meminta Universiti Malaya mengambil tindakan terhadap beliau. Ummi malah diugut, diancam dan dinista. Padahal kata-kata Ummi menistai perbuatan rasuah itu adalah sesuatu yang terpuji.

Setelah ancaman terhadap Ummi menjadi-jadi, Menteri Pendidikan Tinggi Zambry Abdul Kadir akhirnya menegaskan mahasiswa mempunyai hak untuk bersuara dan tiada sebarang tindakan tatatertib akan dikenakan terhadapnya susulan pertanyaan kritis mengenai dana sumbangan Najib itu. Noor Azuan Abu Osman, naib canselor Universiti Malaya turut terpaksa tampil memberikan kenyataan rasmi yang senada.

Kenyataan kedua-dua tokoh besar dalam pengajian tinggi ini amat penting. Ini kerana bekas naib canselor Universiti Malaya antara tahun 1988 sehingga 1991, Syed Hussein Alatas iaitu seorang pemikir, yang karya masyhurnya bertajuk ‘Rasuah: Sifat, Sebab dan Fungsi’ pernah mempopularkan satu terma berkesan. Terma tersebut ialah gejala bebalisme. Ia datang daripada kata bebal, yang secara mudahnya bermaksud bodoh. Malah bebal adalah lebih dahsyat daripada bodoh. Ia adalah satu kalimat yang menunjukkan tumpul otak, sukar mengerti, lambat menanggapi atau memahami sesuatu perkara, dan menurut Dewan Bahasa dan Pustaka membawa juga pengertian melakukan aneka kesalahan berulang.

Akan tetapi apakah yang dimaksudkan oleh Syed Hussein yang terkenal benci rasuah dan perasuah itu dengan kata ‘bebal’. Beliau mula memperkenalkan istilah bebalisme dalam Dewan Masyarakat edisi Mac 1988.

Menurut Syed Hussei, bebalisme ini ‘bukan satu ideologi atau sistem kepercayaan atau kebudayaan atau falsafah’ tetapi ia adalah ‘orientasi pemikiran yang malas, tidak berfikir, tidak berlogik, kadang-kadang kasar, tidak ambil tahu, terlalu cepat percaya tanpa bukti, tidak saintifik, berhamburan, tiada haluan, pasif, tidak kreatif dan tiada tujuan yang terang.’

Semua anasir yang beliau sebutkan di atas akan kita jumpa di media sosial. Kita akan temukan di Facebook, X, Tiktok dan Threads. Apa sahaja yang disalurkan akan diulas sebagai satu komentar, atau ditelan bulat dan lonjong tanpa sebarang daya kritis. Tuduhan, fitnah, dakwaan palsu membiak dan beranak pinak dengan mudah di musim politik bergelora. Gejala bebalisme ini akan mudah dieksploitasi oleh pihak bertentangan dalam politik. Masing-masing akan menyebar informasi yang entah ya entah tidak.

Syed Hussein seterusnya mengatakan ‘bebalisme adalah lintah bagi pemikiran’. Ia tidak perlu diajarkan, atau dikemukakan secara teratur. Ia terjadi dengan sendiri dan ‘disebarkan sebagai satu trend’ dan ia dirujuk sebagai lintah oleh beliau lantaran pelaku atau si bebalis itu ‘bertindak melalui mental tanpa kesedaran’.

Oleh sebab ia adalah lintah bagi pemikiran, ia boleh melekap pada siapa pun. Kata Syed Hussein, ia ‘berada dalam berbagai-bagai golongan masyarakat; tidak kira umur, jantina, kebudayaan, bangsa, agama, falsafah, keadaan, waktu dan tempat’.

Apa yang menggerunkan ia adalah unsur utama yang menghalang pertumbuhan intelektual. Makanya, apabila penyokong Umno ramai-ramai ingin membantai Ummi, kita segera tahu dan mengesani bahawa rata-rata orang Umno ini terkait dengan fenomena bebalisme yang membimbangkan ini. Mungkin tidak semua, misalnya Zambry yang juga ahli Umno.
Syed Hussein juga mengaitkan bebalisme dengan ‘aliran fanatik’ iaitu mereka yang enggan menerima kebenaran dan fakta, dan terus-terusan memilih untuk percaya hal-hal bodoh dan tanpa dasar.
Apakah ciri-ciri bebalisme dan mereka yang menghidapinya, iaitu bebalis?

Menurut Syed Hussein, sang bebalis itu adalah; pertamanya mempertahankan kejahilan dan kedegilan. Keduanya mereka itu pemalas, enggan mengikuti hujah dan menganalisanya. Ketiganya, mereka selalunya bersikap acuh tak acuh, berbanding dengan daya usaha yang gigih dalam berfikir. Yang mana apa sahaja lambakan penipuan dan perdaya akan ‘diterima, berbagai-bagai pendapat, berbagai-bagai khurafat, berbagai- bagai keanehan dan keganjilan’.

Keempat, bebalisme ini menjelma kerana ada rasa diri itu ‘bersifat berkuasa benar (authoritarian) yang mana ini benar pada sesetengah ahli politik yang berasa mereka masih berkuasa atau lebih berkuasa dari rakyat. Itulah sebabnya dalam hal Ummi kita melihat beliau dibuli di dalam talian.
Kelima, mereka yang bebal itu ‘tidak suka merenung dan berfikir dan tidak suka menguji (non-experimental)’.

Keenamnya, tambah Syed Hussein, ‘satu ciri bebalisme adalah menghendaki orang lain mempercayai apa yang disarankan atau diperkatakan tanpa memberi sebab-sebab atau penjelasan yang cukup mengenai sesuatu yang luar daripada kebiasaan’.

Ketujuh, Syed Hussein sosiologis terkemuka negara pernah menulis, ‘bebalisme tidak suka kepada sifat teratur dan perbahasan secara rasional dan tidak menghargai kedua-duanya sama sekali. Apabila seorang bebalis bertindak secara rasional, ini adalah kerana pengaruh daripada kebiasaan dan bukan pemikiran mendalam secara rasional dan kerana terapan agama atau kuasa luar.’ Jika kita merenung ciri ini, kita akan mendapati terdapat sesetengah penyokong agamawan atau tokoh kanan tertentu gagal berfikir waras kerana hati serta penglihatan mereka telah dibutakan oleh ketaasuban.

Kelapan, golongan bebal ini akan cepat kita kesani iaitu ’apabila mereka bertanya, ia menampakkan kurangnya kefahaman mereka tentang prinsip-prinsip dan dengan itu soalan mereka menjadi sia-sia.’ Sebagai contoh dalam hal isu kepimpinan adat dan pertikaian kedudukan Yamtuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, apa sahaja fakta yang dibawa bahawa Undang yang lama telah digantikan di Luak dan disahkan di Dewan Keadilan akan kekal dinafikan, dipermainkan dan ditolak. Mereka enggan berusaha mempelajari prinsip adat sedia ada, dan terus-terusan menghasut, memprovokasi dan mencabar institusi adat dan diraja di negeri itu.

Dan kesembilan, Syed Hussein mengatakan sang bebalis itu biasanya ‘antilogik, kusut pemikiran, subur dengan kurafat, tidak mengandungi rasa seni (unaesthetic), tidak mempunyai sikap memelihara, menerima segala sesuatu tanpa menimbang dengan akal, tidak mempedulikan hukum sebab (causation) dan hukum pertentangan (contradiction), bersikap kuasa-benar (authoritative), dan pemikiran malas, degil, serta buntu.’

Jika kita khuatir gejala bebalisme ini mewabak di Malaysia, kita perlu mengetahui mana asal puncanya. Apakah yang menyebabkan bebalisme ini? Menurut Syed Hussein ia bermula di rumah. Tulis beliau dalam rencana itu, ‘penghalang yang pertama ialah suasana di rumah'. Dalam erti kata lain, jika ibu bapa bodoh dan bengap, biasanya mereka gagal menumbuhkan suasana tidak bebal dalam rumah tangga. Alatas malahan mengatakan untuk mengetahui rumah itu penuh kebebalan atau tidak, memadai dinilai jika ‘keluarga terlalu menggalakkan sukan dan muzik’ dan ‘tidak membaca buku’. Ini kerana ‘pengetahuan intelektual tidak disanjung tinggi sebagaimana pengetahuan tentang agama dan adat’. Syed Hussein seterusnya menyatakan bukanlah setiap rumah perlu melahirkan intelektual; ‘walaupun kita tidak mengharap tiap-tiap orang atau tiap-tiap keluarga melahirkan watak intelektual, tetapi kita perlu berharap sebahagian keluarga dan anggota masyarakat dapat menghasilkan semangat intelektual tadi’.
Apa yang lebih menakutkan dalam masyarakat adalah bebalisme ini turut dibiakkan oleh ahli akademik yang mana itu perlu dibincangkan dalam tulisan lain.

Misalnya, Ketua Menteri Melaka, Ab Rauf Yusoh bakal menerima ijazah kedoktoran daripada Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia (UKM) pada 21 Nov ini. Ketua menteri Melaka yang bakal bergelar doktor itu pernah menyeru penyokong dan rakyat yang menyayangi Najib supaya mengumpulkan dana bagi membantu melengkapkan RM 50 juta agar beliau dapat ditahan di rumah.

Mujur sangat-sangat bekas ketua hakim negara, Tengku Maimun Tuan Mat dilantik sebagai penyandang pertama Kursi Diraja Integriti dan Tadbir Urus Baik, UKM. Pelantikan beliau itu diperkenan dan dititahkan oleh Yang Dipertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz yang juga tersohor antirasuah dan korupsi.

Apa pun syukur nikmat Allah, ada Ummi Umairah Bakhit yang telah dididik dan diasuh di rumah yang betul, di sekolah yang betul, di universiti yang betul; dan membaca bahan-bahan yang betul sehingga mampu berfikir kritis dan tidak bodoh. Sebagai alumni Universiti Malaya saya berbangga dengan Ummi. Tambahan pengungkap kata Syed Hussein adalah sarjana di Universiti Malaya dan pernah menjadi felo penyelidik kanan di Institut Alam dan Tamadun Melayu (Atma) di UKM suatu masa dahulu.
Pun berapa ramai generasi baharu seperti Ummi Umairah Bakhit? Berapa ramai yang mengenali Syed Hussein Alatas. Buka media sosial anda dan lihat berapa dan betapa ramai bebalis di luar sana.

dc2ecfeed8750825: From Moaz Nair

The persistent, fractured politicking among Indian political leaders has devolved into a tragic spectacle of self-preservation, birthing a swarm of toothless, ego-driven factions that have completely abandoned the community’s most vulnerable.
For decades, these leaders have traded genuine community advancement for personal clout and minor cabinet crumbs, leaving working-class Indians politically homeless.

Ironically, as the Indian demographic footprint shrinks, the number of these redundant, self-serving political groups keeps multiplying — each shouting from its own small hill while achieving absolutely nothing of substance.

If these career politicians truly possess an ounce of genuine care for the marginalised, they must immediately halt their petty bickering, dismantle their hollow factions, and focus on delivering institutional, non-negotiable economic welfare.

Recent demographic data from the statistics department covering 2016 to 2026 lays bare a damning reality. In just one decade, the Indian component of the citizen population shrivelled from 7% to 6.5%. Representing roughly 5.8% of the total national population, ethnic Indians total about 2.1 million citizens.
Behind these dwindling percentages lies an unsettling truth: a minority community is fast becoming adrift from the mainstream of national development.

Approximately 38.7% of the community falls into the Bottom 40% (B40) income bracket, translating to 227,000 households. More alarming still, the data indicates that 10% of these B40 families — around 22,000 households — survive on less than RM2,000 a month in extreme precarity.
However, a shrinking population footprint must never be used as a political excuse for a diminished national commitment.

Instead, this demographic decline demands an immediate paradigm shift — shattering the status quo of lazy, generic handouts and replacing them with high-impact policy interventions built upon three non-negotiable pillars.
The 2027 budget attempts to tackle these imbalances, but its success will hinge on execution.
Equity, asset ownership, and economic empowerment

A shrinking population share inherently dilutes purchasing power and locks minority communities out of wealth accumulation. To bridge this widening wealth chasm, outdated asset ownership policies must be aggressively dismantled.
This means enforcing strict, mandatory quotas and dedicated housing funds to guarantee B40 Indian households affordable housing.
The 2027 budget confronts these capital deficits by channelling a combined RM150 million through Tekun Nasional and Amanah Ikhtiar Malaysia.

This includes a dedicated RM100 million Indian Community Entrepreneur Development Scheme to provide critical capital to small business owners, and RM50 million in microcredit loans customised to uplift Indian women entrepreneurs.
Ensuring families own homes and hold financial assets is vital to systematically engineering sustainable, multi-generational social mobility.
TVET overhaul and educational infrastructure

A radical technical and vocational education and training (TVET) overhaul and digital empowerment must disrupt a stagnant workforce. The brutal job market of tomorrow will show no mercy to obsolete skillsets.
Indian youth — particularly those trapped in forgotten suburban fringes and estates — must be aggressively channelled into high-tier TVET ecosystems.

The 2027 budget offers a vital fiscal upgrade here. The allocation for the Malaysian Indian Transformation Unit (Mitra) has been boosted to RM150 million, specifically earmarked to help youths make the transition into high-skilled industrial pipelines. Furthermore, Indian youth must tap into the wider national RM8 billion TVET budget.

Equally foundational is confronting the historical deficits in education infrastructure. Malaysia’s 528 Tamil national-type primary schools (SJKT) carry a complex legacy, with 324 operating as government-assisted institutions sitting on private estate or community trust lands.

This has historically locked many schools out of direct development funding, leaving 68% of them without basic ICT laboratories. The 2027 budget addresses this digital divide with a RM50 million allocation for essential repairs, rewiring, and basic amenities, alongside full reconstruction priorities for severe emergencies like at SJKT Dengkil in Selangor and SJKT Gopeng in Perak.
Ruthless structural reform for targeted poverty alleviation
The survival of these policies hinges entirely on a ruthless structural reform of Mitra. For decades, fragmented agendas and redundant aid distribution have sabotaged state interventions.

Mitra must be stripped of bureaucracy and given absolute, transparent, and centralised power over data, funding, and execution. Armed with a unified database, cost-of-living aid, scholarships, and micro-business grants can finally bypass bureaucratic gridlock.

Crucially, the ultimate success of the budget for working-class Indians relies on broader macroeconomic shifts. The mandated minimum wage hike to RM2,000 per month starting June 2027 will immediately lift the community’s most vulnerable 22,000 households out of deep financial distress, especially when combined with the RM16 billion Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah cash aid pool.
Moving beyond salvation

Ultimately, the integrity of Malaysia’s future will be judged by how it treats its most vulnerable. Addressing this demographic collapse is not a bloodless numbers game on a spreadsheet; it is an urgent battle for socioeconomic justice.
By executing these progressive policy pillars, the country can transform a demographic challenge into a powerful reservoir of human capital.

However, relying solely on external political salvation is a failing strategy. If the Indian community is to survive as a relevant economic force in Malaysia’s shifting landscape, it must aggressively dismantle internal fatalism.

Upward mobility cannot be granted by policy alone. Real transformation demands that the community fiercely engineer its own self-upliftment — taking absolute ownership of its wealth, its trajectory, and its future generations.
Moaz Nair is an FMT reader.
